answers.rationale: Moving frames by reading hardware addresses describes a switch at the Data-Link Layer, not routing between subnets.

answers.text: Gateway names an exterior gateway router, so those devices link Autonomous Systems (ASs).
answers.rationale: Exterior gateway routers move information between Autonomous Systems (ASs), while these devices sit between subnets of one base.

questions.stem: During a Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) review of a base router, an airman finds the auxiliary port set up with a modem for remote configuration, though it has not been used in years. The airman proposes leaving it as a backup way into the router. MSgt Rush must decide the port's status. Which decision is best supported?

keywords.text: auxiliary port set up with a modem for remote configuration

answers.text: Keep the auxiliary port, since remote modem access is a useful backup path.
answers.rationale: A backup path does not outweigh the danger of an unused remote modem port, and a secure installation is what the review enforces.

answers.text: Disable the auxiliary port, since it is often disabled for its inherent security risk.
answers.rationale: The auxiliary port allows remote configuration by modem and should be disabled for security reasons, which fits the standardized secure installation and maintenance a Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) sets.

answers.text: Disable the console port, since it gives direct access to the router.
answers.rationale: The console port gives local, direct access through terminal emulation; disabling it leaves the remote modem path open.

answers.text: Keep the auxiliary port, since Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) scanning software validates it.
answers.rationale: Scanning software validates configuration, but a validated setup of a risky remote port is still a risky remote port.

questions.stem: After a new router passes its Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) scan at installation, an airman proposes closing the STIG work for that router for good. MSgt Rush must decide what the STIG still requires over the router's service. Which decision is best supported?

keywords.text: closing the STIG work for that router for good

answers.text: Close the security work, since passing the scan at installation completes compliance.
answers.rationale: A Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) covers maintenance as well as installation, so a passed installation scan does not end the work.

answers.text: Close the security work, since the guides cover hardware and the router is now installed.
answers.rationale: A Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) applies to computer hardware and software and covers maintenance, so an installed router is still in scope.

answers.text: Continue the security work, since the guidelines span the device's lifecycle with administrative processes.
answers.rationale: A Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) is a methodology for secure installation and maintenance, and its guidelines include recommended administrative processes that span the device's lifecycle.

answers.text: Hand the security work to the scanning software, since it maintains the configuration by itself.
answers.rationale: Scanning software implements and validates configuration; the recommended steps people carry out over the router's life are not done by the software.

questions.stem: Two links connect a squadron to a server farm with similar bandwidth and load, but one shows a high bit-error rate, and packets crossing it are often discarded. An airman wants the routers to keep using that link because it has the fewest hops. MSgt Rush must pick the metric that would steer traffic away from it. Which choice is best supported?

answers.text: Hop count, since it counts the routers that a packet passes through on its way.
answers.rationale: Hop count favors the error-prone link, since it has the fewest hops.

answers.text: Bandwidth, since it rates the available traffic capacity of each of the two links to the server farm.
answers.rationale: The two links have similar bandwidth, so this metric does not separate them.

answers.text: Load, since it measures how busy each network resource, such as a router, is.
answers.rationale: The two links carry similar load, so this metric does not separate them.

answers.text: Reliability, since it rates link dependability by bit-error rate, and bit errors cause discards.
answers.rationale: Reliability rates each link's dependability, usually by bit-error rate, and a bit error that makes the Cyclical Redundancy Check (CRC) incorrect gets the packet discarded.

questions.stem: A router's routing table lists the correct best path to a remote network, yet packets arriving on its inbound interface are not passed to the outbound interface toward that network. An airman proposes rebuilding the routing table. MSgt Rush must name the routing activity that is failing. Which choice is best supported?

keywords.text: not passed to the outbound interface

answers.text: Path determination, since it builds the routing table that the router uses to forward packets.
answers.rationale: Path determination chooses the optimal path, and the routing table already lists the correct best path, so that activity is working.

answers.text: Neighbor discovery, since it lets network devices identify one another.
answers.rationale: Neighbor discovery lets devices identify one another; it does not move a packet from one interface to another.

answers.text: Packet switching, since it transports packets from one router interface to the next.
answers.rationale: Routing involves path determination and the transport of packets through an internetwork, packet switching, which forwards each packet from router interface to router interface.

answers.text: Error reporting, since it returns packet processing problems to the source.
answers.rationale: Error reporting tells the source about processing problems; it is not the activity that moves packets between interfaces.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must pick an interior routing protocol for a very large base network that will be split into groups of contiguous networks, with each group's topology hidden from routers outside it. An airman proposes Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP), since it scales to large networks. Which choice is best supported?

keywords.text: each group's topology hidden from routers outside it

answers.text: Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP), since it scales to large networks with backup routes.
answers.rationale: Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) scales to large networks, but it has no area concept, so it cannot hide each group's topology.

answers.text: Routing Information Protocol (RIP), since its updates go first to directly connected neighbors.
answers.rationale: Routing Information Protocol (RIP) is limited by hop count, which makes it unsuitable for a very large network, and it has no grouping of networks.

answers.text: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), since it exchanges routing information between groups of networks.
answers.rationale: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) exchanges routing information between Autonomous Systems (ASs), not between groups inside one interior network.

answers.text: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), since it divides an Autonomous System (AS) into areas with hidden topologies.
answers.rationale: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) divides an Autonomous System (AS) into areas of contiguous networks, and area topologies are invisible to the backbone and other areas.

questions.stem: Traffic from a base network to outside networks now needs address translation and a firewall. An airman proposes running both on the core routers, since outside requests already cross the core on their way out. MSgt Rush must decide where the two functions go in the hierarchical design. Which placement is best supported?

keywords.text: running both on the core routers

answers.text: Place both on the core routers, since outside requests already cross the core.
answers.rationale: Core devices should not be burdened with processes such as address translation that stand in the way of switching packets at top speed, so the core routers are the wrong place.

answers.text: Place both at the distribution layer, since that layer implements policy tools such as these.
answers.rationale: The distribution layer is the place for policy tools, including address translation and firewalls, while core devices should be spared address translation so they switch packets at top speed.

answers.text: Place both on the access switches, since those switches connect the hosts sending requests.
answers.rationale: Access switches connect multiple desktop devices and are characterized by many ports and low cost; address translation and firewalls are not among the functions listed for this layer.

answers.text: Place both on the core routers over fiber links, since fiber keeps core traffic fast.
answers.rationale: Fiber optics facilitate speed and redundancy, but core devices should still not be burdened with address translation, which stands in the way of switching packets at top speed.

questions.stem: A new wing adds 30 desktop computers and two printers. The building's core switch and its distribution switch both have spare high-speed ports. An airman proposes plugging the desktops straight into the core switch so their traffic reaches the backbone with no extra hop. MSgt Rush must decide how to connect the new devices. Which decision is best supported?

keywords.text: plugging the desktops straight into the core switch

answers.text: Connect them to the core switch, since its spare ports give the desktops the fastest path.
answers.rationale: Connecting devices that belong to the access layer to the core supports workgroup access there, which defeats the concept of the hierarchical model and the core layer.

answers.text: Connect them to the distribution switch, since it aggregates traffic before it reaches the core.
answers.rationale: The distribution layer should avoid functions that belong to one of the other layers, such as desktops, phones and printers, so its spare ports are not for these devices.

answers.text: Connect them through access switches, since the access layer connects workstations and end-user devices.
answers.rationale: The access layer is the aggregation point whose hubs and switches connect workstations to the network, while the core should not support workgroup access and the distribution layer avoids end-user devices.

answers.text: Connect the printers to the distribution switch and the desktops to access switches, since printers are shared.
answers.rationale: Printers are listed with desktops and phones among the functions the distribution layer should avoid, so sharing them does not move them off the access switches.

questions.stem: The base internetwork keeps growing, and traffic through the core layer now slows during peak hours. An airman proposes adding two more routers to the core to share the load. MSgt Rush must decide how to restore core performance. Which plan is best supported?

keywords.text: adding two more routers to the core

answers.text: Add the two routers to the core, since more routers spread the growing load.
answers.rationale: Adding routers expands the core as the internetwork grows, which the core design guidance says to avoid when performance becomes an issue there.

answers.text: Upgrade the existing core devices, since the core should not expand as the network grows.
answers.rationale: When performance becomes an issue in the core, upgrades are preferred over expansion such as adding routers, and an upgrade adds no filtering that slows traffic.

answers.text: Upgrade the core devices and add packet filtering, since dropping low-priority traffic lightens the load.
answers.rationale: An upgrade fits the core guidance, but core layers are designed with speed in mind, and packet filtering there is to be avoided because it slows traffic down.

answers.text: Connect new workgroups straight to the core, since skipping layers shortens the path.
answers.rationale: Connecting workgroup devices that belong to the access layer to the core defeats the concept of the hierarchical model and the core layer.

questions.stem: Last month a single faulty link in the core layer cut users across the base off from the outside world for an hour. MSgt Rush has funding for one improvement, and it must not slow core traffic. An airman proposes adding access lists at the core to block suspect traffic before it reaches that link. Which improvement is best supported?

keywords.text: adding access lists at the core

answers.text: Add access lists at the core, since blocking suspect traffic protects the faulty link.
answers.rationale: Core devices should not be burdened with access-list checking, and blocking traffic adds none of the redundancy that keeps one faulty link from cutting users off.

answers.text: Add redundant fiber optic links in the core, since one core fault can reach users base-wide.
answers.rationale: A failure in the core may affect every user, so fault tolerance there needs redundancy, and fiber optic links facilitate both speed and redundancy.

answers.text: Add more low-cost access switches, since extra ports give users other paths out.
answers.rationale: Access switches are characterized by many ports and low cost for connecting desktops, and adding them still leaves the single core link as the point of failure.

answers.text: Connect key workstations directly to the core, since fewer hops leave fewer links to fail.
answers.rationale: Connecting devices that belong to the access layer to the core defeats the concept of the hierarchical model and the core layer, and it adds no redundancy.

questions.stem: Requests from a squadron's workstations to a remote service are reaching it by a poor path, and the core links show no faults. An airman proposes changing path selection on the core switches, since every request crosses the backbone. MSgt Rush must decide where to act. Which action is best supported?

keywords.text: changing path selection on the core switches

answers.text: Change path selection on the core switches, since the requests cross the backbone.
answers.rationale: The core layer's purpose is to transport large amounts of traffic quickly and reliably; it carries each request after the path is chosen, not before.

answers.text: Review the distribution layer, since it finds the best path before passing requests on.
answers.rationale: All traffic for remote services is handled by the distribution layer, which determines the best path and forwards the request to the core layer for transport.

answers.text: Review the access switches, since the workstations' requests enter the network there.
answers.rationale: The access layer ensures frames are delivered to end user computers; it does not determine the path that remote-service requests take.

answers.text: Add routers to the core, since more routes there give the requests a better path.
answers.rationale: Adding routers expands the core, which is to be avoided as the internetwork grows, and the core transports requests rather than choosing their path.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is adding a new workstation port to the training Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN), and the training VLAN must also exchange traffic with the operations VLAN. An airman proposes handling both tasks on the access switch that the workstation plugs into. Which assignment of the two tasks is best supported?

keywords.text: handling both tasks on the access switch

answers.text: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership at the access layer, and routing between VLANs at the distribution layer
answers.rationale: The access layer includes Layer 2 functions such as Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership, while routing between VLANs is a workgroup support function of the distribution layer.

answers.text: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership at the access layer, and routing between VLANs at the access layer
answers.rationale: Routing between Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) is listed as a workgroup support function of another layer, so the access switch should not take it on.

answers.text: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership at the distribution layer, and routing between VLANs at the distribution layer
answers.rationale: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership is one of the Layer 2 functions listed for the access layer, not one of the distribution policy tasks.

answers.text: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership at the distribution layer, and routing between VLANs at the access layer
answers.rationale: This swaps the two tasks, since Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership is an access layer function and routing between VLANs is a distribution layer function.

questions.stem: Two filtering needs come up in one week. An unknown laptop must be kept off the network by its Media Access Control (MAC) address at the port it uses, and an access list must control traffic passing between two building networks. An airman proposes putting both filters on the core routers so one device enforces everything. Where should MSgt Rush place the two filters?

keywords.text: putting both filters on the core routers

answers.text: Media Access Control (MAC) filtering at the access layer, and the access list at the distribution layer
answers.rationale: Traffic filtering based on Media Access Control (MAC) belongs at the access layer, while access lists and packet filtering are tools implemented at the distribution layer.

answers.text: Media Access Control (MAC) filtering at the distribution layer, and the access list at the access layer
answers.rationale: This swaps the filters, since traffic filtering based on Media Access Control (MAC) is listed for the access layer and access lists are a distribution layer tool.

answers.text: Media Access Control (MAC) filtering at the core layer, and the access list at the core layer
answers.rationale: Core devices should not be burdened with access-list checking or other processes that stand in the way of switching packets at top speed.

answers.text: Media Access Control (MAC) filtering at the access layer, and the access list at the access layer
answers.rationale: The access layer handles traffic filtering based on Media Access Control (MAC), but access lists are a policy tool listed for another layer, not among the access layer functions.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is buying switches for a new building. One set will connect about 40 desktop computers in each wing, and one switch will aggregate the wings' switches and pass their combined traffic toward the core. An airman proposes buying the same many-port low-cost model for both roles to save money. Which purchase plan is best supported?

keywords.text: buying the same many-port low-cost model for both roles

answers.text: Buy many-port low-cost switches for both roles, since one model keeps spares simple.
answers.rationale: The aggregation switch must be capable of handling a large amount of traffic and employs layer 2 and layer 3 devices, a need that low cost and many ports do not address.

answers.text: Buy many-port low-cost switches for the wings and a high-capacity aggregation switch, since the roles differ.
answers.rationale: Access switches connecting desktops are characterized by many ports and low cost, while the distribution switch aggregating them must handle large amounts of traffic.

answers.text: Buy high-capacity switches for both roles, since desktops need the same speed as the core.
answers.rationale: Switches that connect desktop devices to the distribution layer are characterized by many ports and low cost, so high-capacity units for the wings misread that role.

answers.text: Buy high-capacity switches for the wings and a many-port low-cost aggregation switch, since desktops create the traffic.
answers.rationale: This reverses the roles, since wing switches connecting desktops are characterized by many ports and low cost and the aggregation switch must handle large amounts of traffic.

questions.stem: A squadron network was subnetted with one subnet mask, so every subnet holds the same number of hosts. The maintenance shop needs more hosts than its subnet allows, while a small office subnet leaves most of its addresses unused. An airman proposes aggregating the subnets into a larger supernet to recover the unused addresses. MSgt Rush must pick the change that reduces wasted addresses. Which change is best supported?

keywords.text: aggregating the subnets into a larger supernet

answers.text: Aggregate the subnets into a larger supernet, since joined subnets share their unused addresses.
answers.rationale: Supernetting aggregates networks into larger supernets instead of breaking a network into subnets, so it cannot size the shop and office subnets to their own host needs, which is how wasted addresses are reduced.

answers.text: Break the subnets down with more than one mask, since each subnet holds a different number of hosts.
answers.rationale: A network assigned more than one subnet mask has a Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM); any one subnet can be broken down into further subnets, and letting each subnet hold a different number of hosts reduces wasted addresses.

answers.text: Keep the single mask across the subnets, since subnets of equal size waste the fewest addresses.
answers.rationale: Equal subnets ignore what each subnet requires; sizing each subnet to its own host needs is what reduces wasted addresses.

answers.text: Assign the network and broadcast IDs to devices, since those addresses sit unused on each subnet.
answers.rationale: The network ID and broadcast ID are never used when counting the addresses available to assign to devices, so handing them out is not a way to recover addresses.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush tells an airman to divide a squadron's single Internet Protocol (IP) network into smaller portions, one for each flight. The airman proposes supernetting the network, reasoning that supernetting applies the principles of subnetting and so will produce the smaller portions. MSgt Rush must decide whether the proposal fits the task before any addresses change. Which response is best supported?

answers.text: Subnet it by borrowing host bits, since supernetting aggregates networks into larger supernets.
answers.rationale: Subnetting divides a network by borrowing bits from the host portion of the Internet Protocol (IP) address, while supernetting aggregates networks into larger supernets instead of breaking one into subnets.

answers.text: Supernet it as proposed, since supernetting applies subnetting to the portions of one network.
answers.rationale: Supernetting applies the principles of subnetting to larger networks by aggregating them into supernets; it does not divide one network into smaller portions.

answers.text: Supernet it as proposed, since aggregating the flights divides the network into portions.
answers.rationale: Aggregating networks joins them into larger supernets, the opposite of dividing one network into smaller portions.

answers.text: Subnet it by adding bits to the host portion, since a larger host portion leaves room for each flight.
answers.rationale: Subnetting is done by borrowing bits from the host portion of the Internet Protocol (IP) address, not by adding bits to it.

questions.stem: An airman is planning the addressing for a new squadron building and picks the subnet mask that yields the most subnets, to leave room for future shops. One shop already needs many hosts on a single subnet. The airman claims each subnet keeps the same host count however many bits are borrowed. MSgt Rush must review the plan before it is used. Which assessment is best supported?

keywords.text: picks the subnet mask that yields the most subnets

answers.text: Base the design on subnet and host needs, since more borrowed bits leave fewer hosts per subnet.
answers.rationale: Designing a simple network is based on how many subnets and how many hosts each subnet needs, and more bits borrowed means fewer addressable hosts, so a mask chosen for the most subnets can starve the large shop.

answers.text: Base the design on subnet needs alone, since each subnet keeps its host count as bits are borrowed.
answers.rationale: More bits borrowed means fewer individually addressable hosts, so the host count does change, and the shop's need for many hosts makes host needs part of this design.

answers.text: Base the design on host needs alone, since the subnet mask does not set how many subnets exist.
answers.rationale: The subnet mask tells how many bits are borrowed, which is how many subnets the network has, so the mask does set the subnet count.

answers.text: Assign the network and broadcast IDs to the shop's devices, since that adds hosts to its subnet.
answers.rationale: The network ID and broadcast ID are never used when counting the addresses available to assign to devices, so they cannot add hosts to the shop's subnet.

questions.stem: Before a new building wing is cabled, the airmen installing it need one drawing that tells them which category of twisted pair cable to run to each office and which numbered port on each switch every cable plugs into. MSgt Rush must assign the diagram the airman on the design cell will produce. Which choice is best supported?

keywords.text: which numbered port on each switch every cable plugs into

answers.text: Produce a logical network diagram, since it shows the subnets and routing protocols between devices.
answers.rationale: A logical network diagram typically shows subnets, network devices such as routers and firewalls, and routing protocols, not the twisted pair category or the port each cable plugs into.

answers.text: Produce a physical network diagram, since it can show the cable category and labeled port numbers.
answers.rationale: A physical network diagram shows the actual arrangement of cables and hardware, can name the twisted pair category, and may label port numbers so you know which port to plug each cable into.

answers.text: Produce a data flow diagram, since it shows the data sources, destinations and flows of the system.
answers.rationale: A data flow diagram illustrates data sources, destinations, flows, stores and transformations of a system; it does not show twisted pair categories or device ports.

answers.text: Produce a procedure specification, since it details the actual steps to accomplish a specific task.
answers.rationale: A procedure specification details the steps and path control of a procedure on a data flow diagram, not the twisted pair category or the port each cable plugs into.

questions.stem: An airman on the help desk must often look up a device's Internet Protocol (IP) address while troubleshooting the squadron network. MSgt Rush also wants the same drawing to record each subnet's Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) ID and mask and the routing protocols in use. Which diagram should the airman maintain to meet both needs?

keywords.text: look up a device's Internet Protocol (IP) address while troubleshooting

answers.text: Maintain a physical network diagram, since it shows the cables, hardware and labeled port numbers.
answers.rationale: A physical network diagram shows the actual arrangement of cables and hardware; subnets with Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) IDs and masks and routing protocols are shown on a logical diagram.

answers.text: Maintain a data flow diagram, since it shows how data moves between the processes and data stores.
answers.rationale: A data flow diagram illustrates data sources, destinations, flows, stores and transformations of a system, not Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) IDs, masks or routing protocols.

answers.text: Maintain a logical network diagram, since it lays out the subnets, addresses and routing protocols.
answers.rationale: Logical network diagrams typically show subnets with Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) IDs, masks and addresses plus routing protocols, and their address layout is a handy troubleshooting reference.

answers.text: Maintain a procedure specification, since it details the actual steps of each troubleshooting task.
answers.rationale: A procedure specification details actual procedures and the control over which path to take; it does not record Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) IDs, masks or routing protocols.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush asks an airman to document a supply request system. The drawing must show the sources of requests that sit outside the system boundary and where request records are kept while they are not moving; cables, ports and addresses do not matter. The airman suggests a logical network diagram because it describes how information flows. Which response is best supported?

keywords.text: sources of requests that sit outside the system boundary

answers.text: Use a logical network diagram, since it describes the way information flows through a network.
answers.rationale: Logical network diagrams describe information flow through a network with subnets, routers and routing protocols; they do not represent external entities or data stores of a system.

answers.text: Use a data flow diagram, since it represents the external entities and data stores of a system.
answers.rationale: A data flow diagram illustrates data sources, destinations and stores, and must represent external entities outside the system boundary and data stores for data that is not moving.

answers.text: Use a physical network diagram, since it shows the actual arrangement of the system's components.
answers.rationale: A physical network diagram shows the arrangement of cables and hardware, which the stated need excludes, and it does not represent external entities or data stores.

answers.text: Use a procedure specification, since it details the data manipulation that each task performs.
answers.rationale: A procedure specification details actual steps and the control over which path to take, not the sources outside the system boundary or the data at rest.

questions.stem: An airman's data flow diagram for a leave request system presents the possible paths a request can take. MSgt Rush now needs a written record of how the system selects the specific path that a given request follows. The airman proposes adding that path selection logic to the data flow diagram itself. Which response is best supported?

keywords.text: how the system selects the specific path

answers.text: Record the path selection on the data flow diagram, since it already presents the possible paths.
answers.rationale: A data flow diagram presents all possible paths, but control, or how to select a specific path, is not shown on it.

answers.text: Record the path selection in a procedure specification, since a data flow diagram does not show control.
answers.rationale: Control, or how to select a specific path, is not shown on a data flow diagram; a procedure specification details actual procedures, including control over which path to take.

answers.text: Record the path selection on a lower level of the data flow diagram, since leveling adds more detail.
answers.rationale: Leveling shows different detail on hierarchical levels of the data flow diagram, but control is not shown on the data flow diagram.

answers.text: Record the path selection on a logical network diagram, since it describes how information flows.
answers.rationale: A logical network diagram describes information flow through a network; it does not detail the steps or path control of a procedure.

questions.stem: On a star network, every workstation in an office loses network access at the same moment, although each machine still powers on and runs its programs. The airman on duty proposes reimaging the workstations one by one. MSgt Rush wants the most likely point of failure checked first. Which assessment is best supported?

keywords.text: loses network access at the same moment

answers.text: The workstations themselves, since one crashed machine in a star brings down the others.
answers.rationale: Star topologies tend to be reliable because individual machines may crash without affecting the rest, so a simultaneous loss points away from the workstations.

answers.text: The central hub or switch, since the connected nodes lose access when it fails.
answers.rationale: Individual machines in a star may crash without affecting the rest, but if the central hub or switch fails, none of the connected nodes will be able to access it.

answers.text: The cable to one workstation, since one break takes a whole star network down.
answers.rationale: A whole-network outage from one break describes the central bus of a bus topology; in a star, each peripheral node connects to the central node.

answers.text: The linear bus backbone, since star workstations attach to it in segments.
answers.rationale: Star-configured segments on a linear bus backbone describe a tree topology, and this office is a plain star network.

questions.stem: An airman documents a network in which several groups of star-wired workstations each hang off a single linear bus backbone. The draft labels the layout a hybrid topology because it mixes two topologies. MSgt Rush must approve the label before the drawing is filed. Which response is best supported?

keywords.text: star-wired workstations each hang off a single linear bus backbone

answers.text: Label it a tree topology, since a bus and star combination is not counted as a hybrid.
answers.rationale: The tree topology is star-configured segments connected to a linear bus backbone; a combination that is not bus and star is what the hybrid label covers.

answers.text: Label it a hybrid topology, since a hybrid is a combination of two different topologies.
answers.rationale: A hybrid is any combination of topologies except bus and star; a bus and star combination is a tree topology.

answers.text: Label it a star topology, since each workstation group has its own central node.
answers.rationale: Each segment is star-configured, but the segments also join a linear bus backbone, which a star topology does not describe.

answers.text: Label it a bus topology, since the groups share one central medium with two endpoints.
answers.rationale: A bus connects all nodes by one central medium with two endpoints, but these workstations sit in star segments on the backbone, which is a tree.

questions.stem: An airman's physical network diagram shows a single Cat5e run of 130 meters between two switches in neighboring buildings. The airman plans to keep the run because the diagram already names the cable category. MSgt Rush must decide whether the drawing can be approved as drawn. Which response is best supported?

answers.text: Approve the run as drawn, since the diagram already names the cable category it uses.
answers.rationale: Naming the category does not settle distance: each cable type has a maximum distance, and Cat5e is limited to 100 meters (328 feet) between devices.

answers.text: Revise the run to meet Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards, since Cat5e past its maximum distance degrades the signal.
answers.rationale: Cat5e has a maximum distance between devices, past which it suffers signal degradation, and Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards are used when developing these diagrams to ensure proper cable type and distance.

answers.text: Approve the run as drawn, since Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards cover connector types and not cable distance.
answers.rationale: Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards do cover connector types, but they are also used to ensure the proper cable type and distance, so the over-length run fails them.

answers.text: Revise the connectors to RJ45, since the connector type sets the maximum distance of a run.
answers.rationale: Certain cables need specific connectors such as RJ45, but each cable type has its own maximum distance, so new connectors leave the over-length run unchanged.

questions.stem: An airman reviews an office where each workstation is cabled to one central switch, a physical star. The airman's notes claim that Ethernet on this network cannot operate as a bus, because the cabling is not laid out as a bus. MSgt Rush must correct the notes before they are filed. Which correction is best supported?

keywords.text: cannot operate as a bus, because the cabling is not laid out as a bus

answers.text: Ethernet is a logical bus here, since logical topology follows network protocols, not cabling.
answers.rationale: Logical topology is bound to network protocols, unlike physical topology, and Ethernet, the best-known logical bus, is associated with physical bus, star and tree topologies.

answers.text: Ethernet is a logical star here, since a logical topology copies the physical cabling layout.
answers.rationale: The main difference between the two is that logical topology is bound to the protocols in use, and Ethernet is the best-known example of a logical bus.

answers.text: Ethernet needs physical bus cabling here, since a logical bus works on bus cabling alone.
answers.rationale: Ethernet is associated with physical bus, star and tree topologies, so star cabling does not stop it from operating as a logical bus.

answers.text: Ethernet is a full mesh here, since each node can reach the other nodes through the switch.
answers.rationale: In a full mesh each node is directly connected to every other node; workstations cabled to one central switch form a star.

questions.stem: While checking an Ethernet segment cabled as a physical bus, an airman sees that a file sent from one workstation to a server also reaches every other device on the segment. The airman suggests the other devices are misconfigured and should be rebuilt before the problem spreads. MSgt Rush must explain what those devices are doing. Which explanation is best supported?

keywords.text: also reaches every other device on the segment

answers.text: The devices are misconfigured, since a sender delivers its data straight to one destination.
answers.rationale: On a logical bus, each time a device has data to send it broadcasts the data to the entire network, so other devices hearing it is expected.

answers.text: The devices are working normally, since each checks the data and ignores what is not for it.
answers.rationale: On a logical bus the sender broadcasts data to the entire network, and the devices look to see if it is for them, keeping it if so and ignoring it if not.

answers.text: The devices are colliding, since several of them are taking in the same data at once.
answers.rationale: A collision happens when more than one device transmits at the same time; devices hearing one sender's data are not transmitting, so they are not colliding.

answers.text: The devices are forwarding the data, since a logical bus passes data on toward the server.
answers.rationale: Devices that hear data not meant for them ignore it; the sender has already broadcast it to the entire network.

questions.stem: Two workstations on an Ethernet segment transmit at the same moment and their frames collide. An airman proposes that both should resend at once so that no time is lost. MSgt Rush must describe how Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) handles the retry. Which description is best supported?

keywords.text: transmit at the same moment and their frames collide

answers.text: Both resend at once, since collision detection rules clear the line right away.
answers.rationale: If more than one device transmits at the same time there is a collision, and both devices wait a random amount of time to retransmit, not resend at once.

answers.text: Both wait a random time and listen for other traffic before sending again.
answers.rationale: After a collision both devices wait a random amount of time to retransmit, and under carrier sense all devices listen before transmitting.

answers.text: Both wait a fixed time and send again without listening for other traffic.
answers.rationale: The wait after a collision is a random amount of time, and carrier sense requires every device to listen before transmitting.

answers.text: Both resend at once, since carrier sense lets each one hear the line is clear.
answers.rationale: Carrier sense means listening before transmitting, but after a collision both devices still wait a random amount of time before they retransmit.

questions.stem: An airman's notes for a logical network diagram must name where the rules for detecting and responding to collisions are defined, and the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer where Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (CSMA/CD) originates. The airman proposes the Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards and the Network layer, since logical network diagrams correlate with layer 3. Which entry is best supported?

keywords.text: where the rules for detecting and responding to collisions are defined

answers.text: The Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards, with an origin at Layer 3
answers.rationale: Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards ensure the proper cable type and distance, and the layer 3 link describes logical diagrams; the access method itself originates at the Data Link layer.

answers.text: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3 rules, with an origin at Layer 2
answers.rationale: Collision detection and response are defined within the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3 rules, and the access method originates at the Data Link layer and is implemented at the Physical layer.

answers.text: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3 rules, with an origin at Layer 3
answers.rationale: The rule source is right, but logical diagrams correlating with layer 3 does not move the access method; it originates at the Data Link layer.

answers.text: The Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards, with an origin at Layer 2
answers.rationale: The layer is right, but Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) standards ensure the proper cable type and distance and cover connector types, not how devices detect and respond to collisions.

questions.stem: In a small office, every frame that one computer sends shows up at all the other computers on the same device. Which device connects them?

keywords.text: shows up at all the other computers

answers.rationale: A hub copies each frame that enters one interface and repeats it out all other interfaces.
A switch forwards a frame only out the interface tied to the destination host once that address is in its table.
A router is a Layer 3 device that forwards packets between networks, not a device that repeats every frame.
A Layer 3 switch combines Layer 2 switching with routing, so it forwards known frames out one interface only.

questions.stem: On a switched network with redundant links, frames meant for every device keep getting resent onto the link until no device can communicate. Which problem has the network developed?

keywords.text: frames meant for every device keep getting resent onto the link

answers.rationale: A broadcast storm is broadcast data that other devices keep rebroadcasting onto the link until the whole network is overwhelmed.
Multiple frame copies means one device receives the same frame from different Local Area Network (LAN) segments, not network-wide failure.
Multiple loops are loops occurring within other loops in the network, not frames for every device being resent.
A late collision is another system transmitting after a host has sent at least 64 bytes of its frame.

questions.stem: Frames from Switch A still reach Switch B over their cable, but frames from Switch B no longer reach Switch A. Which problem has developed on the cable?

keywords.text: frames from Switch B no longer reach Switch A

answers.rationale: A unidirectional link occurs when traffic in one of two directions on a link fails, for example from a bad transmitter.
A late collision is a transmission by another system after a host has sent at least 64 bytes, not a one-way failure.
Multiple frame copies means a device receives the same frame from different segments, not that one direction stops.
A broadcast storm is broadcast data rebroadcast until the whole network is overwhelmed, not traffic failing in one direction.

questions.stem: A host has already sent 200 bytes of its frame when another system on the same shared bandwidth starts to transmit. What does this indicate?

keywords.text: already sent 200 bytes of its frame

answers.rationale: A late collision indicates another system attempted to transmit after a host had sent at least the first 64 bytes of its frame.
Fragmentation is most likely within the first 64 bytes of a frame, and this transmission started well after them.
A broadcast storm is rebroadcast data overwhelming the whole network, not one system transmitting during a host's frame.
A unidirectional link is traffic failing in one of two directions on a link, not two systems transmitting at once.

questions.stem: A switch's address table already lists Host C beside interface 4, and a frame for Host C arrives on interface 1. What does the switch do with it?

keywords.text: already lists Host C beside interface 4

answers.rationale: When the destination is already listed in the table, the frame is forwarded only out the interface identified with that host.

answers.text: Floods it out other active ports
answers.rationale: A frame is flooded out all active interfaces except the receiving one only when its destination is not yet in the table.

answers.text: Discards it and alerts the sender
answers.rationale: A frame is discarded with an error message to the sender when an error check finds an error, not because its host is listed.
Unidirectional Link Detection (UDLD) shuts down the port of a switch having trouble hearing, which is not this case.

questions.stem: A newly cabled file server transmits for the first time, and the switch's table now shows the server beside the interface it is cabled to. Which switch function did this?

keywords.text: the switch's table now shows the server beside the interface

answers.rationale: Address learning places a transmitting device's source address in the table along with the interface ID it is connected on.
The forward/filter decision uses entries already in the table to send a frame out one interface; it does not create them.
Loop avoidance deals with more than one path to a destination device, not with recording where a device is connected.
Flooding sends a frame for an unknown destination out all active interfaces except the receiving one; it records nothing.

questions.stem: Finance and Sales computers share one switch but sit in separate Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), and no Sales computer receives Finance frames. Which benefit is this?

keywords.text: no Sales computer receives Finance frames

answers.rationale: Only devices in the same Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) receive the frame, which is how VLANs increase security.
Flexibility comes from adding or limiting devices in a broadcast domain regardless of physical location, not from keeping frames from other offices.
Removing the geographical barrier lets one virtual network span separate physical segments; it does not keep frames from other offices.
Wire speed is a switch setting matched to the media (cable) speed, not a result of grouping the Finance computers.

questions.stem: Frames reach an airman's computer from a squadron switch with their Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) tags already removed. What kind of port delivers them?

answers.rationale: The tag is removed when a frame is placed on an access port, which is also called an untagged port.
Trunks are also called tagged ports: a tag is applied when a frame crosses a trunk, not removed.
A console port is used for a networking device's initial configuration, not for delivering frames to computers.
An auxiliary port lets an administrator configure a router remotely using a modem, not deliver frames to computers.

questions.stem: A squadron router must link the base network to a distant site over a Wide Area Network (WAN) circuit. Which kind of router connection should the airman configure?

keywords.text: link the base network to a distant site

answers.rationale: Synchronous serial interfaces are configured to allow connection to Wide Area Networks (WANs), such as a link to a distant site.
Token Ring interfaces are configured for a Local Area Network (LAN) connection, not for a Wide Area Network (WAN) link.
The console port gives local, direct access for configuring the router, not a link to a distant site.

questions.stem: An airman wants to check the configuration a router is using right now and its current routing tables. Which router memory holds both?

keywords.text: configuration a router is using right now

answers.rationale: Random Access Memory (RAM) is the router's working memory and contains the running-configuration file and the routing tables.
Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) stores the startup-configuration file, not the configuration in use or the routing tables.
Flash memory holds the Internetwork Operating System (IOS), not the running configuration or the routing tables.
Read Only Memory (ROM) is not where the router keeps the running configuration or the routing tables.

questions.stem: A base's finance office and supply office each have their own Local Area Network (LAN), and one router passes traffic between them. Which router type is it?

keywords.text: each have their own Local Area Network (LAN)

answers.rationale: An interior router is a router in a single Local Area Network (LAN), not one that joins two LANs.
A border router connects a Local Area Network (LAN) with the Wide Area Network (WAN), not one LAN with another.
Exterior gateway routers move information between Autonomous Systems (ASs), not between two Local Area Networks (LANs) at one base.

questions.stem: Each of five sites troubleshoots its own routers with its own tools, and no one can support the whole internetwork from one place. Which internetworking challenge is unmet?

keywords.text: troubleshoots its own routers with its own tools
support the whole internetwork from one place

answers.rationale: Network management calls for centralized support and troubleshooting capabilities for the internetwork, which the separate sites lack.
Connectivity is about supporting communication between very different technologies, not about where support and troubleshooting happen.
Reliable service is about consistent, reliable access to network resources, not about central support and troubleshooting.
Flexibility concerns network expansion or contraction and new applications and services, not central support and troubleshooting.

questions.stem: A packet travels from a host through three routers to a server on a distant network. Which addresses in the packet stay the same at every hop?

keywords.text: stay the same at every hop

answers.rationale: The Network Layer Internet Protocol (IP) source and destination addresses remain constant as the packet moves through the internetwork.
The Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses are the ones that change as the packet travels through the network.
The Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses change as the packet travels, so not both kinds stay the same.
The Internet Protocol (IP) source and destination stay the same, so one kind of address does stay constant.

questions.stem: A misconfigured route sends a packet back and forth between two routers until one router finally discards it. Which header value ran out?

keywords.text: back and forth between two routers

answers.rationale: A packet is discarded when its Time to Live (TTL) counter expires while it is being routed through the network.
A wrong version number gets a packet discarded, but it is not a value that runs out while the packet circulates.
An incorrect Cyclical Redundancy Check (CRC) comes from a bit error during transmission, not from a value running out.
The allow fragmentation flag matters only when a packet must be fragmented; it is not a value that runs out.

questions.stem: A host has a server's Internet Protocol (IP) address on its segment but still needs the server's Media Access Control (MAC) address to send a frame. Which protocol supplies it?

answers.rationale: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) resolves an Internet Protocol (IP) address to a Media Access Control (MAC) address.
Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) reports errors about Internet Protocol (IP) packet processing back to the source; it does not resolve addresses.
Routing Information Protocol (RIP) is a distance vector routing protocol between routers, not a way to learn a host's hardware address.
Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) is a link state routing protocol that shares link states, not host hardware addresses.

questions.stem: A router learns paths to one destination network from both Routing Information Protocol (RIP) and Open Shortest Path First (OSPF). Which value decides which source the router prefers?

keywords.text: from both Routing Information Protocol (RIP) and Open Shortest Path First (OSPF)

answers.rationale: With paths from more than one routing source, routers choose the lowest Administrative Distance, the more trustworthy route.
Hop count counts the devices a packet passes through; it does not rate how trustworthy a routing source is.
Path length is the sum of the link costs along a path, not a rating of the routing source.
Communication cost reflects the operating expense of lines, not how trustworthy a routing source is.

questions.stem: An administrator sends a test packet along each of two paths and records which one arrives at the server sooner. Which routing metric is being compared?

keywords.text: records which one arrives at the server sooner

answers.rationale: Delay is the length of time required to move a packet from source to destination, which the arrival test compares.
Hop count is the number of internetworking devices a packet passes through, not the time it takes to arrive.
Bandwidth is a link's available traffic capacity, and greater bandwidth does not necessarily mean the better route.

questions.stem: A base is moving its routers to IPv6 and wants to keep a Routing Information Protocol (RIP) distance vector design. Which protocol was made for this move?

answers.rationale: RIPng, the next generation of Routing Information Protocol (RIP), the distance vector protocol, was developed for IPv6.
RIPv1 is the original version of Routing Information Protocol (RIP), and it was not developed for IPv6.
RIPv2 improved Routing Information Protocol (RIP), but it is not the version that was developed for IPv6.
Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) is a link state protocol, so OSPFv3, although it supports IPv6, is not a distance vector design.

questions.stem: A better path to a remote network comes online, but a router keeps its old path until an administrator changes it by hand. Which routing approach is it using?

answers.rationale: Static routes are established by the network administrator and do not change until the administrator changes them.
Dynamic routing recalculates routes when routing messages report a network change, so the router would adopt the better path itself.
Link state routers send updates when link status changes, so the router would learn the new path without an administrator.
Distance vector routers send updates at regular intervals and for changes, so the new path would be learned automatically.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is ordering equipment for the layer that carries traffic common to most users across the base. Which devices normally fill this layer?

keywords.text: carries traffic common to most users

answers.rationale: The core carries traffic common to most users, and its devices are normally high-speed switches and routers.
Hubs and many-port, low-cost switches that connect workstations belong to the access layer, not the core.
Desktop computers and printers are end-user devices reached through access switches, not equipment that carries core traffic.
Firewalls and packet filtering are distribution layer policy tools; the core avoids filtering so it does not slow traffic.

questions.stem: A building's access switches are being retired, and an airman suggests cabling its desktop computers directly to the core switches. Which core design consideration warns against this?

keywords.text: cabling its desktop computers directly to the core switches

answers.rationale: Workgroups says the core should not support workgroup access by connecting devices that belong to the access layer, such as desktop computers.
Speed warns against slowing core traffic with Access Control Lists (ACLs), routing and packet filtering, not against attaching desktops.
Reliability and Redundancy calls for fast, redundant media such as fiber optics, not a rule on which devices connect.
Protocols covers routing protocols with low convergence times and keeping extra processing off core devices, not which devices attach to the core.

questions.stem: An airman is setting up the distribution switch that joins a building's access switches to the core. Which job belongs on this switch?

answers.rationale: The distribution layer is where policy tools such as access lists, packet filtering, address translation and firewalls are implemented.
Desktops connect through access switches, and the distribution layer avoids functions that belong only to other layers, such as PCs.
The core is the high-speed backbone; the distribution switch aggregates access switches and must handle large amounts of traffic.
Shared bandwidth devices are listed among the access layer functions, not the distribution layer policies.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush needs new switches to connect the workstations along one office corridor. Which trait marks switches at this layer of the hierarchical model?

answers.rationale: Handling large amounts of traffic suits the distribution switch that aggregates access switches, not switches for desktops.
Fast, redundant media such as fiber optics are a core layer design consideration, not a trait of desktop switches.
Access layer switches connect multiple desktop devices to the distribution layer and are characterized as having many ports and low cost.
Redistributing between routing protocols is a distribution layer task, not a trait of switches that connect desktops.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush borrows more bits from each Internet Protocol (IP) address to give the squadron's network extra subnets. What happens to each subnet?

answers.rationale: The bits are borrowed from the host portion, and more bits borrowed means fewer individually addressable hosts.
Joining networks into larger supernets is aggregation; borrowing bits breaks one network into subnets instead.
A subnet mask is what shows how many bits are being borrowed, so each subnet still needs one.

answers.text: It gets a longer host portion
answers.rationale: The borrowed bits come out of the host portion, so each subnet's host portion gets shorter, not longer.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush can read a workstation's Internet Protocol (IP) address but cannot tell how many of its bits belong to the network portion. Which value shows this?

keywords.text: how many of its bits belong to the network portion

answers.rationale: The network ID is the first host ID of a subnet, reserved for the network; it does not mark the network bits.
The broadcast ID is the last host ID of a subnet, reserved for broadcasts; it does not mark the network bits.
The host ID range is the addresses between the network ID and broadcast ID; it does not mark the network bits.

questions.stem: On the squadron's Internet Protocol (IP) network, the headquarters subnet and the shop subnets each use a different mask. What does the network use?

answers.rationale: A network assigned more than one subnet mask is said to have a Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM).
Classful routing makes every router in the network use the same subnet mask, so the masks could not differ.
A Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) groups devices into a single broadcast domain; it says nothing about the masks used.
Supernetting aggregates networks into larger supernets; it does not describe the masks inside one network.

questions.stem: One break in the single shared cable that links every office computer took the whole network down. Which topology does the office network use?

answers.rationale: A star topology passes all data through a central hub or switch, not along one shared cable.
A full mesh topology connects each node directly to every other node, not through one shared cable.
When the central bus of a bus topology breaks down, so does the whole network.
A partial mesh topology connects nodes to the nodes they interact with most, not through one shared cable.

questions.stem: An airman plans a Cat5e run from a wiring closet to an office several times farther away than Cat5e is rated to reach. What problem should MSgt Rush expect?

keywords.text: several times farther away than Cat5e is rated to reach

answers.rationale: Each cable type has a maximum distance it can be used without suffering signal degradation.
Frame copies arrive when one frame reaches a device from different segments at once, not from cable length.
A loop is more than one path to a destination device, which one long run does not create.

questions.stem: A router on one subnet stopped passing traffic, and an airman needs that subnet's addresses and mask before testing it. Which document should the airman open?

answers.rationale: A physical network diagram shows the cables and hardware, not the addresses and mask of each subnet.
A data flow diagram illustrates data sources, destinations, flows, stores and transformations, not subnet addresses.
Logical network diagrams lay out Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and subnets, a handy reference when troubleshooting.
A procedure specification details the steps of a specific task, not subnet addresses and masks.

questions.stem: While reviewing a payroll data flow diagram, MSgt Rush asks how often the report process is run each week. Which detail is being requested?

keywords.text: how often the report process is run

answers.rationale: Control is how to select a specific path, not how often a report is produced.
Leveling represents different detail levels on hierarchical views, not how often a report is produced.
Repetition is how many times or when a procedure is performed, which a data flow diagram does not include.
Data flows show movement of data in the system, not how often a report is produced.

questions.stem: During a video call, frames cross several office switches and the users notice almost no delay at any point. Which switch performance feature does this describe?

answers.rationale: Wire speed means a port can be configured to the media (cable) speed, not that switches add little lag.
Broadcast control means switches segment networks, which limits where broadcasts go rather than how quickly data is processed.
Hardware-based bridging is the use of Application Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) to form internal connections, not the lag measure itself.

questions.stem: A switch is powered on and tests its own hardware before it loads any Operating System (OS). Which component holds the routines it runs first?

answers.rationale: Read Only Memory (ROM) is burned in memory that contains the diagnostic and boot up routines.
Flash memory saves the Operating System (OS) itself, which the switch loads into running memory as it boots up.
Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) saves the startup-configuration and other long-term information, not diagnostic routines.
Random Access Memory (RAM) is not burned-in memory, so it does not hold the routines that run first.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush links two routers with one dedicated cable and needs a Layer 2 protocol for just those two devices. Which protocol fits?

answers.rationale: Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) is a data link layer protocol that establishes communication directly between two network devices without relying on any host.
Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) lets switches discover physical loops; it does not establish communication between two devices.
Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) lets devices advertise data and configurations to adjacent nodes, not establish their communication.
Unidirectional Link Detection (UDLD) makes a switch having trouble hearing shut down the port; it does not establish communication.

questions.stem: For backup, an airman runs a second cable between two Layer 2 devices that one cable already joins. What does the network now contain?

keywords.text: runs a second cable between two Layer 2 devices

answers.rationale: A switching loop is more than one path to a destination, and multiple links between switches create loops.
A unidirectional link occurs when traffic in one of two directions on a link fails, not when a cable is added.
A late collision is another system transmitting after a host has sent at least 64 bytes, not a cabling layout.
Multiple links between switches are used to overcome a single point of failure, not to create one.

questions.stem: A core switch must pass frames on with the least possible delay, and occasional bad frames reaching hosts are acceptable. Which switching method should it use?

answers.rationale: Cut-Through switching reduces latency, although bad frames are forwarded, and it works best at the core layer where speed is important.
Store-and-Forward stores the entire frame and checks it for errors before forwarding, so it does not give the least delay.
Fragment-Free stores the first 64 bytes before forwarding, so it waits longer than a method that copies only the destination address.
Adaptive switching selects the best method based on traffic conditions; it is not itself the lowest-delay method.

questions.stem: Two computers cabled to the same hub begin sending frames at exactly the same moment. What is the result?

answers.rationale: When two system transmissions occur at the same time on shared bandwidth, such as a hub's, the result is a collision.
A late collision is a transmission after a host has already sent at least the first 64 bytes, not one starting together.
A broadcast storm is broadcast data rebroadcast until the whole network is overwhelmed, not two frames sent at once.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sees that every Sales computer receives each hello packet that any Sales computer sends to all devices. What does the Sales Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) form?

keywords.text: receives each hello packet that any Sales computer sends to all devices

answers.rationale: A Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) groups devices into a single broadcast domain, where every connected device sees every broadcast.
Each switch port is its own collision domain because it shares no bandwidth, so a whole virtual network is not one.
An internetwork is routers in different networks connected together, not computers that all see one another's broadcasts.
A trunk is a connection between network devices that carries more than one virtual network, not a group of computers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush logs on to a squadron switch from his desk with telnet to change its settings. Which kind of Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) carries that session?

answers.rationale: The management Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) is used for purposes such as telnet, which logs on to a device remotely.
Best practice keeps data traffic separate from in-band traffic such as telnet, so the data type is not the one asked for.
Voice is a separate type of virtual network, not the one listed for purposes such as telnet.
An inactive Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) holds unused ports that are shut down, so it carries no telnet session.

questions.stem: A workstation must send a file to a server on a different network, so it first hands the packet to a router. Which host setting names that router?

keywords.text: first hands the packet to a router

answers.rationale: The default gateway is the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the nearest router interface, the host's access point to or from a network.
A subnet mask is used to extract the subnet address, not to name the router a host uses to leave its network.
The physical or Media Access Control (MAC) address sends information between Layer 2 interfaces, not toward a router on another network.
A local broadcast reaches all computers on the network segment, not a router address for other networks.

questions.stem: An airman moves a network printer from a router's first interface to its second interface. Which hosts can now receive the printer's broadcast messages?

keywords.text: router's first interface to its second interface

answers.rationale: Each router interface is a separate broadcast domain, so the printer's broadcasts reach the hosts that share its new interface.
Broadcasts stop at the router, so hosts on the old interface, now a different network, no longer receive them.
Each router interface is a separate broadcast domain, so a broadcast does not cross from one interface to the other.
A local broadcast is received by all computers on the network segment, so hosts sharing the printer's interface receive it.

questions.stem: An older base network still sends user data between its subnets in Internet Packet Exchange (IPX) packets, which its routers forward. Which protocol type is IPX?

keywords.text: sends user data between its subnets

answers.rationale: Internet Packet Exchange (IPX), like Internet Protocol (IP) and AppleTalk, is a routed protocol that routers forward using its logical addressing.
Routing protocols handle path determination and build routing tables; they are not the protocol whose packets carry user data.
Interior Gateway Protocols are what interior gateway routers use to exchange information within an Autonomous System (AS), not user data.
Exterior Gateway Protocols move information between Autonomous Systems (ASs); they are a routing protocol family, not the protocol carrying user data.

questions.stem: A router receives a packet for a network that appears nowhere in its routing table, yet still forwards it upstream. Which route did it use?

keywords.text: appears nowhere in its routing table

answers.rationale: A default route is a special static route that a router uses when no route to the destination is known.
A dynamic route is learned through a routing protocol for a known destination, but this destination is not known.
Routers know directly connected networks through working interfaces, so a connected destination would not be unknown.
A feasible successor is a backup route to a known destination in a topology table, not a path for unknown destinations.

questions.stem: A base network gives its links subnet masks of several different lengths, and every router must learn those masks from routing updates. Which protocol cannot support this design?

keywords.text: subnet masks of several different lengths
learn those masks from routing updates

answers.rationale: RIPv1 cannot use subnet masks of varying lengths, because its routing updates do not include subnet mask information.
RIPv2 includes subnet mask data in all routing updates, so it allows subnet masks of varying lengths.
Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) includes subnet masks with each advertised destination, enabling masks of varying lengths.
Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) exchanges subnet mask information in its updates, so masks of varying lengths are supported.

questions.stem: When one of its connections goes down, a router tells routers well beyond its neighbors about just that connection. Which routing approach is it using?

answers.rationale: Link state algorithms notify the other routers in the routing area about the status of their connected links and send small updates everywhere.
Distance vector routers send their entire routing table, and only to their neighbors, not one link's status to routers beyond them.
Path vector routing is the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) approach for exchanging routing information between Autonomous Systems (ASs), not within one area.
Static routes are set by the network administrator and do not change until the administrator changes them, so no notice is sent.

questions.stem: An airman compares two Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routers in the same area. Which of their data structures should match exactly?

keywords.text: two Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routers in the same area

answers.rationale: Routers within the same area share the same information, so they have identical topology tables of Link State Advertisements (LSAs).
Each neighbor table records the addresses and interfaces of that router's own neighbors, so two routers' entries differ.
Each router calculates its own shortest-path tree with itself as the root, so the trees differ between routers.
An Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache stores the addresses a device has resolved, not shared Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) data.

questions.stem: An Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) router loses its best path to a server network and switches to a second path it already chose. What is that path called?

keywords.text: a second path it already chose

answers.rationale: In the Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) topology table, the feasible successor is the backup route to a destination.
The successor is the best route, the one this router just lost, not the second path it switches to.
A default route is a special static route for destinations with no known route, but this destination was known.
A static route is manually configured by the system administrator, not chosen by the routing protocol as a second path.

questions.stem: Two Internet service providers exchange routes, and each provider's administrators manually set the rules for choosing paths. Which routing protocol works this way?

keywords.text: Two Internet service providers exchange routes
manually set the rules for choosing paths

answers.rationale: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) bases routing decisions on network policies that network administrators input manually, not on metrics.
Routing Information Protocol (RIP) rates routes by hop count, a metric, not by administrator-set policies.
Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) chooses routes by a cost metric based on interface bandwidth, not by administrator-set policies.
Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) uses bandwidth and delay as default metrics, not administrator-set policies.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush checks that a squadron's routers were set up and are kept patched exactly as Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) documents prescribe. Which documents set that standard?

keywords.text: set up and are kept patched

answers.rationale: A Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) is the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) methodology for standardized secure installation and maintenance.
National Security Agency (NSA) Guides are a separate configuration standard, not the guides the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) provides.
A startup-configuration file is one router's stored configuration in Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM), not an agency standard.
The Internetwork Operating System (IOS) is the router software held in flash memory, not a standard for secure installation.

questions.stem: To test a link, an airman pings a server, and the server answers each echo request with an echo reply. Which protocol generates these messages?

keywords.text: echo request with an echo reply

answers.rationale: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) generates Echo Request and Echo Reply messages; ping sends an ICMP echo request to the destination.
Ping tests Internet Protocol (IP) through the network, but IP itself does not generate the echo request and reply messages.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps Internet Protocol (IP) addresses to Media Access Control (MAC) addresses; it does not generate echo messages.
Hello messages and replies let routers discover neighbors; they are not the echo request and reply that ping uses.

questions.stem: During a busy duty day, a cable in the high-speed backbone fails. Which users may this failure affect?

keywords.text: a cable in the high-speed backbone fails

answers.rationale: A failure in the core layer, by a faulty link or device, may affect every user, which is why core redundancy is essential.
Traffic carried across the core is common to most users, so a core fault is not limited to one access switch.
Core traffic is common to most users across the network, so a core fault reaches well beyond one building.
The core does not serve single workgroups; the traffic it carries is common to most users.

questions.stem: The base network has doubled in size, and an airman proposes three more routers in the backbone to carry the load. Which core design consideration warns against this?

keywords.text: three more routers in the backbone

answers.rationale: Scalability says to avoid expanding the core, such as adding routers, as the internetwork grows, and to prefer upgrades.
Speed warns against slowing core traffic with Access Control Lists (ACLs), routing and packet filtering, not against adding routers.
Workgroups warns against connecting access layer devices to the core; routers added to carry backbone load are not such devices.
Protocols covers choosing routing protocols with low convergence times, not how many routers the core holds.

questions.stem: Desktops in the supply Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) must reach a printer in the finance VLAN. Which layer should pass traffic between these two VLANs?

keywords.text: pass traffic between these two VLANs

answers.rationale: The core avoids routing when possible so it does not slow traffic; it only transports large amounts of traffic quickly.
Routing between Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) is a workgroup support function listed among the distribution layer policies.
The access layer gives ports Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) membership; passing traffic between VLANs is not among its functions.
The core avoids routing when possible, and the access layer functions do not include routing between Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is setting up the switch that connects one office's desktop computers to the network. Which job belongs on this switch?

answers.rationale: Redistributing between routing protocols, including static routing, is a distribution layer policy task.
Traffic filtering based on Media Access Control (MAC) addresses is one of the functions that should be included at the access layer.
Address translation is a distribution layer policy tool, and core devices should not be burdened with it.
The core is the high-speed backbone; access switches connect desktop devices to the distribution layer.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush combines several of the base's small networks into one larger network. Which term names this approach?

keywords.text: combines several of the base's small networks into one larger network

answers.rationale: Aggregating networks into larger supernets is Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR), which is often referred to as supernetting.
Subnetting divides one network into smaller portions called subnets; it does not combine networks.
