answers.rationale: Every electronic device gives off signals, and monitoring the electrical signals a computer emits can expose information even when it is not networked.

answers.text: The airman is wrong, since signals come from devices designed as transmitters, and the workstation contains one.
answers.rationale: A device gives off signals whether or not it was designed as a transmitter, so the reasoning given is not why the workstation needs review.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must connect two buildings with a wire line that will carry unencrypted information in a facility where the threat level is high. An airman proposes a plain, unprotected cable run to save time. Which design is best supported?

answers.text: A simple distribution system, since it permits unencrypted information with a reduced level of physical protection.
answers.rationale: A simple distribution system gets only a reduced level of physical security protection, which does not match a high threat level.

answers.text: A plain cable run, since a wire line needs no safeguards to carry unencrypted information.
answers.rationale: A wire line may carry unencrypted information only through a protected distribution system that includes adequate safeguards.

answers.text: A hardened distribution system, since it adds significant physical protection such as an alarmed carrier.
answers.rationale: A protected distribution system permits unencrypted transmission, and the hardened category is afforded significant physical protection, which suits a high threat level.

answers.text: Red/black separation alone, since it partitions plain-text signals from encrypted signals on a wire line.
answers.rationale: Red/black separation partitions signals in cryptographic systems; it is not a safeguarded line that permits unencrypted transmission.

questions.stem: A facility plans to replace some copper links between classified and unclassified equipment with fiber-optic cabling and keep the rest. An airman asks whether the new links will still need red/black separation. MSgt Rush must answer for the fiber links and for the remaining copper links. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: answer for the fiber links and for the remaining copper links

answers.text: Yes for both, since the separation depends on the classification of the signals rather than the cabling type.
answers.rationale: Red/black separation does not apply to fiber optics systems, whatever the classification of the signals they carry.

answers.text: No for the fiber links, since fiber optics systems are exempt, and yes for the copper links, which still need it.
answers.rationale: Red/black separation is a copper cabling principle that does not apply to fiber optics, and it stays relevant for copper links.

answers.text: No for both, since encrypting the signals on the copper links makes the separation unnecessary.
answers.rationale: Red/black separation partitions plain-text signals from encrypted ones on copper cabling, so encryption elsewhere does not remove the need.

answers.text: Yes for the fiber links, since light waves carry plain-text signals, and no for the copper links.
answers.rationale: Fiber optics systems are exempt from red/black separation, and the separation continues to be relevant for copper-based cabling.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush handles two tasks for a new classified contract: deciding whether the airmen and the company's staff are eligible to access classified information, and protecting classified information released to the company under the contract. Which pairing of core disciplines is best supported?

answers.text: Industrial security for the eligibility decisions and personnel security for the information released to the company.
answers.rationale: The disciplines are reversed: personnel security determines eligibility, and industrial security protects information released to industry.

answers.text: Personnel security for the eligibility decisions and Operations Security (OPSEC) for the information released to the company.
answers.rationale: Operations Security (OPSEC) is not a core discipline of Information Protection; industrial security protects information released to industry.

answers.text: Personnel security for the eligibility decisions and industrial security for the information released to the company.
answers.rationale: Personnel security determines eligibility to access classified information, and industrial security protects classified information released to industry under classified contracts.

answers.text: Information Security (INFOSEC) for the eligibility decisions and industrial security for the information released to the company.
answers.rationale: Information Security (INFOSEC) protects classified information and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI); personnel security is the discipline that determines eligibility.

questions.stem: A Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request from the public asks for a unit recall roster listing personnel telephone numbers and home addresses. MSgt Rush must decide how to respond. Which response is best supported?

keywords.text: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request from the public

answers.text: Release it, since the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) gives the public the right to request records from federal agencies, whatever the record holds.
answers.rationale: The right to request records is subject to nine exemptions, and releasing personal addresses falls under the privacy exemption.

answers.text: Withhold it as Secret information, since personal contact details need classified protection.
answers.rationale: The roster is unclassified personal information, so a classification level such as Secret does not fit it.

answers.text: Withhold it, since the privacy exemption applies and the roster can carry the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) designation.
answers.rationale: Exemption 6 covers a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, and a recall roster qualifies under it and can be designated Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).

answers.text: Release it with the addresses removed, since exemptions apply to classified records rather than personal privacy.
answers.rationale: Exemptions protect interests such as personal privacy, not only classified records, so the stated reason is false and the roster falls under Exemption 6.

questions.stem: An airman proposes mailing a package of Top Secret documents by U.S. Postal Service registered mail within the 50 states, noting that registered mail is approved for Secret information. MSgt Rush must respond. Which response is best supported?

keywords.text: mailing a package of Top Secret documents

answers.text: Approve the plan, since the means for Top Secret are included in Secret and registered mail is available for Secret.
answers.rationale: The inclusion runs the other way: Secret may use the Top Secret means, but registered mail is added only at the Secret level.

answers.text: Reject the plan, since registered mail is added at the Secret level and Top Secret has its own approved methods.
answers.rationale: Registered mail appears only in the Secret list, while Top Secret information shall be transmitted by an approved crypto system, designated cleared U.S. military personnel or the Diplomatic Courier Service.

answers.text: Approve the plan with registered mail, since two opaque sealed envelopes make the mail acceptable.
answers.rationale: Two opaque envelopes describe how mailed classified information is wrapped, not which methods may carry Top Secret.

answers.text: Reject the plan, since registered mail is reserved for Confidential information.
answers.rationale: Registered mail is added at the Secret level, so it is not reserved for Confidential information, and it is not on the Top Secret list either.

questions.stem: An airman hand-carrying a Secret document must stop overnight and suggests locking it in the hotel room safe, which has a combination lock. MSgt Rush must decide where the document is kept. Which action is best supported?

answers.text: Lock it in the hotel room safe, since a combination lock makes the safe an approved container.
answers.rationale: Classified material will not be stored in hotel safes, whatever kind of lock they have.

answers.text: Keep it in the airman's luggage in the hotel room, since a carried document may stay with its carrier overnight.
answers.rationale: During overnight stops classified material is stored at military facilities, embassies or other cleared facilities, not in a hotel room.

answers.text: Store it at a military facility in a security container approved for Secret, since hotel safes are not used.
answers.rationale: Overnight stops use military facilities, embassies or other cleared facilities, and Secret must be stored in a General Services Administration (GSA) container approved for its level.

answers.text: Store it in an unlocked desk at a government building, since building security is provided.
answers.rationale: Unlocked desks after hours are allowed for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) with building security, but classified material needs an approved security container.

questions.stem: Before a deployment, an airman plans to post battle-scene photographs from a prior tour on social media and to text the unit's departure date to a contact. MSgt Rush must advise on both plans. Which advice is best supported?

answers.text: Post the photographs but do not text the date, since the departure date is the critical information in the plans.
answers.rationale: Publishing photographs that display critical or sensitive information is itself one of the easiest ways for adversaries to gather information.

answers.text: Text the date but do not post the photographs, since a text message is a private channel.
answers.rationale: Text messages can be intercepted by an unintended party, so texting the departure date still exposes it.

answers.text: Do both, since the photographs show past events and a text message goes to a trusted contact.
answers.rationale: Photographs displaying critical information should not be published, and text messages remain open to interception whatever the recipient.

answers.text: Do neither, since the photographs display critical information and text messages can be intercepted over the air.
answers.rationale: Social media is one of the easiest ways for adversaries to gather information, and Short Message Service (SMS) messages can be intercepted over the air.

questions.stem: An adversary watches a base and notes extra aircraft fueling and loading activity at the flight line. None of this is secret, but together it reveals when a mission will launch. MSgt Rush must label these observations under Operations Security (OPSEC) terms. Which label is best supported?

keywords.text: together it reveals when a mission will launch

answers.text: The observations are critical information, and the launch time they reveal is an indicator.
answers.rationale: The roles are reversed: the observations are the detectable actions pieced together, and the launch time is the fact adversaries need.

answers.text: The observations are indicators, and the launch time they reveal is critical information.
answers.rationale: Friendly detectable actions that an adversary pieces together are indicators, and the launch time is a fact about friendly activities vitally needed by adversaries.

answers.text: The observations are Essential Elements of Friendly Information (EEFI), and the launch time is an indicator.
answers.rationale: Essential Elements of Friendly Information (EEFI) are details such as equipment types or specifications, not detectable actions pieced together.

answers.text: The observations are indicators, and the launch time they reveal is a Critical Information and Indicators List (CIIL).
answers.rationale: A Critical Information and Indicators List (CIIL) is the record that commanders approve, not a fact an adversary derives.

questions.stem: After the commander delegates the Operations Security (OPSEC) program to lower-level squadron personnel, those personnel draft the unit's Critical Information and Indicators List (CIIL). An airman asks who approves the list and who retains responsibility for risk management decisions. Which answer is best supported?

answers.text: The lower-level squadron personnel who drafted it approve the list and retain the risk decisions once the program has been delegated to them.
answers.rationale: Commanders must approve the list, and the commander retains risk management decisions even when program responsibility is delegated.

answers.text: The commander approves the list, but the squadron personnel who run the program take over the risk decisions.
answers.rationale: Delegating program responsibility does not move risk management decisions; the commander retains them.

answers.text: The commander approves the list and retains responsibility for risk management decisions, even though the program was delegated.
answers.rationale: Once a list is developed, commanders must approve it, and the commander retains responsibility for risk management decisions after delegation.

answers.text: The lower-level squadron personnel approve the list, but the commander retains the risk management decisions.
answers.rationale: Approval of the list is the commander's task, so the squadron personnel who drafted it cannot approve it.

questions.stem: An airman needs to send classified materials to another base. The unit's secured systems are available, but the airman sends the materials over an unclassified network instead. MSgt Rush must name the Communications Security (COMSEC) failure and the correction. Which entry is best supported?

answers.text: A cryptosecurity failure, corrected by selecting the proper secured system for the transmission.
answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity concerns the proper use of cryptographic systems; choosing the wrong transmission system is a different component.

answers.text: A Transmission Security failure, corrected by creating a stronger encryption system.
answers.rationale: Transmission Security (TRANSEC) cannot protect against cryptanalysis, and the fault here was the choice of transmission system, not the strength of the encryption.

answers.text: A cryptosecurity failure, corrected by creating a stronger encryption system.
answers.rationale: The fault was the choice of transmission system, not the use or strength of the encryption, so a stronger encryption system would not correct it.

answers.text: A Transmission Security failure, corrected by selecting the proper secured system for the transmission.
answers.rationale: Sending classified materials over an unclassified network is a Transmission Security (TRANSEC) failure, and the measures select the right secured system for the communications need.

questions.stem: An airman tells someone who is not authorized to receive it which model of cryptographic equipment the unit uses and how it is configured. MSgt Rush must identify what the airman put at risk. Which finding is best supported?

answers.text: Transmission Security (TRANSEC), since choosing the wrong transmission system exposed the message to an unintended listener.
answers.rationale: The airman did not choose a transmission system for a message; a conversation exposed information, which concerns how cryptographic systems are used.

answers.text: Cryptanalysis, since the airman tried to break the unit's coding system.
answers.rationale: Cryptanalysis is the science of trying to break a coding system, not something the airman did by describing equipment.

answers.text: Cryptosecurity, since proper use includes withholding equipment details from an unauthorized person.
answers.rationale: Proper cryptosecurity demands never revealing information about equipment such as type and configurations to an unauthorized person.

answers.text: Physical security, since someone viewed Communications Security (COMSEC) material directly.
answers.rationale: The stem describes a spoken description to someone, not unauthorized viewing or possession of material.

questions.stem: An adversary intercepts a message that the unit encrypted. The adversary tries to break the coding system to reveal the information, while the intended receiver restores the message to its original plain text using the correct means. MSgt Rush must name each activity. Which pairing is best supported?

keywords.text: tries to break the coding system

answers.text: The adversary's effort is decryption, and the receiver's restoration is cryptography.
answers.rationale: Decryption is the restoration of encrypted data to a usable state, not an adversary's effort to break the coding system, and cryptography is the use of coding systems generally.

answers.text: The adversary's effort is cryptanalysis, and the receiver's restoration is decryption.
answers.rationale: Cryptanalysis is the science of trying to break a coding system, and decryption is the restoration of encrypted data to its original plain text.

answers.text: The adversary's effort is encryption, and the receiver's restoration is cryptanalysis.
answers.rationale: Encryption is converting data into an unreadable form and cryptanalysis is an effort to break the coding system, so both labels are reversed.

answers.text: The adversary's effort is cryptography, and the receiver's restoration is encryption.
answers.rationale: Cryptography is the use of coding systems, and encryption converts data into a form others cannot easily understand, which is the opposite of restoring it.

questions.stem: An airman uses a program to place a text file inside a graphic file and sends the graphic to a receiver. A second airman says the first airman encrypted the file. MSgt Rush must assess the claim. Which assessment is best supported?

keywords.text: place a text file inside a graphic file

answers.text: Correct, since encryption is the method that hides information inside a graphic file.
answers.rationale: Encryption puts information in an unreadable format until an authorized person decrypts it; hiding information inside a graphic file is steganography.

answers.text: Incorrect, since hiding a text file in a graphic file is steganography, not encryption.
answers.rationale: Steganography is a method of hiding information, such as a text file, in a graphic file, while encryption puts the information in an unreadable format until it is decrypted.

answers.text: Incorrect, since hiding a file in a graphic is hashing, which checks that data was not altered.
answers.rationale: Hashing runs data through an algorithm to produce a hash value that checks integrity; it hides nothing inside a graphic, so naming it as the method is wrong.

answers.text: Correct, since a digital signature places the file inside the graphic and proves the sender.
answers.rationale: A digital signature uses the sender's private key to prove who sent a message; it does not place a file inside a graphic, so the claim rests on the wrong method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must mark a document after the unit's review concludes that unauthorized disclosure of its contents could reasonably be expected to cause serious damage to national security. An airman asks to read it and has the appropriate clearance eligibility and a need to know, but has not signed a Standard Form (SF) 312. Which handling is best supported?

keywords.text: has not signed a Standard Form (SF) 312

answers.text: Mark it Top Secret, since serious damage is the highest level, and give the airman access because the airman has a need to know.
answers.rationale: Top Secret disclosure could cause exceptionally grave damage, which is a greater level than the serious damage described, and access still requires a signed Standard Form (SF) 312.

answers.text: Mark it Confidential, since serious damage is the lowest level, and give the airman access because the airman has clearance eligibility.
answers.rationale: Confidential disclosure could cause some damage to national security, which is less than serious damage, and clearance eligibility alone does not grant access.

answers.text: Mark it Secret and withhold access until the airman signs a Standard Form (SF) 312.
answers.rationale: Disclosure of Secret information could cause serious damage, and access is granted only to an individual with clearance eligibility, a signed Standard Form (SF) 312 and a need to know.

answers.text: Mark it Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and give the airman access because the airman has clearance eligibility and a need to know.
answers.rationale: Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is a designation, not a classification, and a document whose disclosure could damage national security is classified.

questions.stem: Messages sent to the finance office list a trusted base office as the sender, yet they actually came from an outside mailbox. Which STRIDE threat does this show?

keywords.text: list a trusted base office as the sender

answers.rationale: Pretending to be something or someone other than yourself describes the outside mailbox presenting itself as a trusted office.
Tampering modifies something on a disk, network or memory; the stem reports no modification of any data.
Disclosure gives information to someone not authorized to have it; the stem describes no data reaching unauthorized readers.
Elevation lets someone do something beyond their authorization; the stem reports no extra permissions being gained.

questions.stem: Logs show an airman's own account and workstation deleted a shared folder, yet the airman denies ever deleting it. Which STRIDE threat does this show?

answers.rationale: Spoofing is pretending to be another identity; the stem places the airman's own workstation and account at the deletion.
Tampering modifies data on a disk or network; the dispute here is about who acted, not about altered data.
Claiming you did not do something or were not responsible fits an airman disowning the deletion his account performed.
Disclosure gives information to someone not authorized to have it; the stem reports no information reaching anyone.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's visible-to-the-world web servers stall under floods of traffic carrying falsified sender addresses. Which countermeasure may lower this risk?

answers.rationale: Annual training informs users about pitfalls; it does not stop floods of traffic aimed at a server.
Extra sign-in factors protect accounts after a compromise; they do not slow floods aimed at servers.
Checking logs shows signs of compromise afterward; it does not reduce the flood itself.
Packet filtering to prevent obviously forged packets from entering the network address space may reduce the risk of such floods.

questions.stem: The same text message, apparently from a bank, reaches thousands of unrelated people and asks them to confirm account numbers at a web link. Which attack type is this?

answers.rationale: Fraudulent solicitation by text message, often broadcast to a wide audience, acquires sensitive data such as bank account numbers.
This type targets a specific individual or group with tailored messages; the message here goes to thousands of unrelated people.
Whaling is aimed at high-value individuals; the recipients here are ordinary, unrelated people.
Baiting uses curiosity or greed to trigger a trap; the stem describes a request to confirm account details.

questions.stem: An email names an airman, cites a hobby from a public social media page and asks that a form be opened. Which attack type is the most specific fit?

keywords.text: cites a hobby from a public social media page

answers.rationale: Phishing is the broader category; this message targets one named airman, so a narrower type fits.
Spear phishing targets a specific individual by sending messages that appeal to that person, using details from public sources.
Whaling is aimed at high-value individuals; nothing in the stem shows a high-value target.
Baiting uses curiosity or greed to trigger a trap; the stem describes a message tailored to one airman.

questions.stem: Code hidden inside a monitoring tool stays dormant until a particular account is removed from the directory, then disables the nightly backups. Which virus type is this?

keywords.text: stays dormant until a particular account is removed

answers.rationale: A boot-sector virus loads into memory on every startup; the stem's code stays dormant until a triggering event.
A file infector activates any time its host program is used; the stem's code waits for a different trigger.
A logic bomb contains code that will not execute until a certain event occurs, such as a specific date or an account removal.
A macro virus is triggered automatically when a file is opened; the stem's code waits for a different trigger.

questions.stem: The portal turns away an airman who typed a correct username but a wrong password. Which part of Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) rejected the logon?

answers.rationale: Identification is only presenting a username, and the username here was correct.
Authorization grants access after verification, but this logon failed before any access was granted.
Accounting logs usage such as access time and bandwidth; it does not decide whether to accept a logon.
Authentication verifies that individuals are who they say they are, so the wrong password fails here.

questions.stem: A hallway sensor lets an airman through after matching the airman's habitual walking style, not a body feature, to a stored sample. Which factor category does that match use?

answers.rationale: Something you are is a physical characteristic read by a biometrics system, not a habit of movement.
Something you know is a remembered password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), which the hallway sensor never asks for.
Habits such as typing pattern, signature or gait are something you do.
Somewhere you are is the user's location by Global Positioning System (GPS) or Internet Protocol (IP) address, not how the airman moves.

questions.stem: An airman logs on once at shift start, then opens the mail and file servers with no further credential prompts. Which security concept does this show?

answers.rationale: With Single Sign-On (SSO), users authenticate once and reach multiple systems without additional credentials.
Multifactor authentication combines two or more factors at one logon; it does not remove later prompts.
Network Access Control (NAC) gates network access on conditions systems must meet, not repeated credential prompts.
Accounting logs user activity and tracks usage; it does not carry a logon across servers.

questions.stem: An airman taps a smartcard on a door reader; the reader now has a name but has checked nothing. Which part of Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) is done?

keywords.text: has a name but has checked nothing

answers.rationale: Authentication would validate the presented card, but the reader has checked nothing yet.
Authorization grants access after the account information is verified, which has not happened yet.
Accounting logs user activity and tracks usage, which is not presenting a card.
Identification is presenting information about yourself, such as a username or smartcard.

questions.stem: An attacker types hidden code into a public comment box, and every later visitor's browser runs it. Which application vulnerability is this?

keywords.text: every later visitor's browser runs it

answers.rationale: Cross-site request forgery reuses a user's unexpired cookies through another page, not code injected into a comment box.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) uses JavaScript to inject malicious code into a web application.
ActiveX controls need a user to agree to run them, which visitors here never do.
Peer-to-peer file sharing moves files between users, not code typed into a web page.

questions.stem: A workstation keeps starting from a flash drive until an airman changes one entry in the Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) setup program. What did that entry determine?

answers.text: Which storage device boots the system
answers.rationale: The Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) setup program in the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) determines which storage device the system boots from.
Digitally signed bootup files are the Secure Boot feature, not the choice of starting device.

answers.text: Which keys encrypt the hard drive
answers.rationale: Full Disk Encryption (FDE) keys protect the whole drive, not the choice of starting device.
Cryptographic processors sit on an add-on card, which is unrelated to the choice of starting device.

questions.stem: Squadron workstations send web requests to one server, which fetches each page from the Internet and returns the response to the requesting workstation. Which firewall type is that server?

keywords.text: fetches each page from the Internet and returns the response to the requesting workstation

answers.rationale: A forward proxy takes the client request, retrieves the resource on the Internet and sends the response back to the client.
A reverse proxy carries requests in the other direction, from a system on the Internet to an internal server.
A packet-filtering firewall only blocks or allows traffic by address and port; it does not fetch pages for clients.
A stateful firewall filters by address, port and conversation context; it does not fetch pages for clients.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush and an airman open the same site through the proxy minutes apart; the second load finishes sooner than the first. Which proxy feature explains this?

keywords.text: the second load finishes sooner than the first

answers.rationale: Caching stores requested web pages, so the next client gets the page faster without retrieving it from the Internet.
Web filtering limits which websites can be visited; it does not make a repeated page load faster.
The daily log records which websites were visited; it does not supply the page again.
Authentication decides from the username whether a user may use the Internet; it does not speed up pages.

questions.stem: A squadron mail server must accept messages from any outside sender on the Internet. Where does the firewall plan place it?

keywords.text: accept messages from any outside sender on the Internet

answers.rationale: The Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) is where servers that the public must reach, such as a mail server, are placed.
The firewall in front of the private zone sends it no traffic from any other network, so outside senders could not reach a server there.
The guest zone serves visitors who need only Internet access, not a server that every outside sender must reach.
An extranet includes servers made accessible to selected organizations, not to any outside sender.

questions.stem: Before a drill, one member of the response group reminds everyone of their duties and phones an outside agency it might need. Which role in that group fits this member?

answers.rationale: Assessing the situation and its scale does not match reminding everyone of their duties or phoning an outside agency.
Logging each incident and its cause does not match reminding everyone of their duties or phoning an outside agency.
The team leader ensures every member knows their role and builds relationships with outside resources for special circumstances.
Knowing the laws and regulations for forensics does not match reminding everyone of their duties or phoning an outside agency.

questions.stem: A member of the response group examines the affected hosts and reports how widespread the problem is. Which team role fits this member?

answers.rationale: Making sure everyone knows their role and building outside relationships does not match examining hosts and reporting how widespread the problem is.
Knowing the laws and regulations for forensics does not match examining hosts and reporting how widespread the problem is.
Logging each incident and its cause does not match examining hosts and reporting how widespread the problem is.
The Technical Specialist has the expertise to assess the situation and identify the scale of the security incident.

questions.stem: An outsider obtained the password of a server administrator and signed in to a base file server. Which event or incident category applies to this activity?

answers.rationale: Unauthorized access to account credentials that could perform administrative functions is a root-level intrusion.
User-level intrusion is unauthorized non-privileged access; the stolen password here belongs to an administrator.
Malicious logic requires adversary software to be installed; the outsider here only used a stolen password.
An unsuccessful attempt is defeated by normal defenses and never gains access; the outsider here signed in.

questions.stem: Firewall logs show an outsider's hostile upload to a base server was rejected by standard protections, so the attacker never reached the system. Which event or incident category applies?

answers.rationale: Malicious logic is adversary software that was installed; here the hostile upload was rejected and nothing was installed.
A deliberate attempt that normal defensive mechanisms defeat, so the attacker fails to gain access, is an unsuccessful activity attempt.
User-level intrusion requires unauthorized access to be gained; here the attacker never reached the system.
Non-compliance involves action or inaction by authorized users; here an outsider attacked and the attack was stopped.

questions.stem: A reporting server with two drives keeps running with no data lost after MSgt Rush pulls one drive. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) technique was configured?

answers.rationale: Each drive is an exact duplicate of the other, so the remaining drive still holds all the data.
Data divided between two drives boosts performance, but losing either drive loses all the data.
Rebuilding lost data from a parity bit needs at least three disks, more than these two drives.
Two redundant disks need at least four disks, more than this server has.

questions.stem: Each night's backup of a file server runs longer than the last, and the archive bit stays set on every file. Which backup technique is running?

keywords.text: the archive bit stays set on every file

answers.rationale: Everything changed since the most recent complete copy is backed up each time, so every run takes longer.
Every file and folder is copied each time, so run length would not grow night by night.
Only data changed since the previous backup is copied, so each run stays relatively fast.
Vaulting is a method of conducting backups, not a type whose runs grow with data changed since the weekend.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush restores a server by loading the weekend's complete copy and then every nightly copy, in the order the copies were made. Which backup technique made the nightly copies?

keywords.text: every nightly copy, in the order the copies were made

answers.rationale: Each copy holds only data changed since the previous backup, so a restore must replay every one in order.
A restore needs only the most recent complete copy and the latest nightly copy, not a chain.
Each complete copy holds everything, so no later copies need replaying.
Vaulting is a method for conducting backups and does not define a chain of nightly copies.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must set the backup schedule and type for a rarely edited archive whose loss would be serious. Which two factors should drive the policy?

keywords.text: rarely edited archive whose loss would be serious

answers.text: Criticality and rate of new information
answers.rationale: Frequency and type are based on data criticality and how often new information is introduced.
These requirements guide the method of conducting backups, not how often or which type runs.
Size and cost guide the choice of backup media, not the schedule or type.
Policies designate where data is stored and how files are named, which does not set frequency or type.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's workstation sends a report together with a result an algorithm computed from it; the receiver recomputes the result to compare. What is the sent result called?

keywords.text: the receiver recomputes the result to compare

answers.rationale: A digital signature is created with the sender's private key to prove the sender; the stem describes a compared result, not a proof of sender.
A digital certificate is an electronic file that transports keys; the stem describes a computed result, not a file of keys.
The sending system runs the data through a hashing algorithm, and the answer, the hash value, travels with the data for comparison.
Cipher text is encrypted data; the attached result in the stem is compared, not decrypted.

questions.stem: On payday, users cannot open the payroll system because its service is down. Which security goal does this outage fail?

answers.rationale: Confidentiality is about who may read information; the stem reports no unauthorized reader.
Integrity is about data staying unaltered; the stem reports no changed data.
Availability ensures the information can be reached when the user wants it, and an outage during payday breaks that.
Nonrepudiation is about disputing a sent message or change; the stem reports no dispute.

questions.stem: In a crypto room, MSgt Rush must keep circuits that carry plain-text classified signals from running beside circuits that carry encrypted signals. Which countermeasure does this apply?

keywords.text: keep circuits that carry plain-text classified signals

answers.rationale: A protected distribution system adds safeguards so a line may carry unencrypted information; it does not route two kinds of signals apart.
Shielding is a protective measure around equipment; it does not partition signal types by circuit.
A simple distribution system is a carrier with reduced physical protection; it does not route signal types apart.
Red/black separation partitions signals with sensitive plain-text information, red signals, from those carrying encrypted information, black signals.

questions.stem: A review finds that unauthorized release of a memo would harm national security, though at the lowest of the three classification levels. Which marking applies?

keywords.text: lowest of the three classification levels

answers.rationale: Secret requires a substantial degree of protection, and its disclosure could cause serious damage, which is above the lowest level.
Confidential classification is given to information needing less protection than Secret or Top Secret; disclosure could cause some damage to national security.
Top Secret requires the highest degree of protection, and its disclosure could cause exceptionally grave damage, the highest level.
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is a designation for unclassified information, not one of the classification levels.

questions.stem: An airman has clearance eligibility and a need to know, but MSgt Rush withholds access to a classified file. Which requirement is the airman still missing?

keywords.text: clearance eligibility and a need to know

answers.rationale: Access requires clearance eligibility, a signed Standard Form (SF) 312, the Classified Information Nondisclosure Agreement, and a need to know.
A Security Classification Guide (SCG) is the preferred way for original classification authorities to issue classification guidance; it is not an access requirement.
Original Classification Authority (OCA) is delegated to certain Air Force officials for classifying information; holding it is not required to read classified information.
Derivative classifiers receive initial and refresher training for marking the documents they create, which is separate from the requirements for access.

questions.stem: An adversary never sees the deployment date written anywhere, yet infers it from a public vendor order and a parking change. Which Operations Security (OPSEC) term names those clues?

keywords.text: infers it from a public vendor order and a parking change

answers.rationale: Critical information is the fact adversaries need, such as the deployment date, not each clue they piece together.
Classified information is protected under classification levels; the clues in the stem are open to the public.
An open conversation is talk in a public area or online where others may listen; the stem describes an order and a parking change.
A friendly detectable action or open-source information that an adversary pieces together to derive critical information is an indicator.

questions.stem: At home, an airman tells relatives with no clearance the unit's departure date and destination. Which Operations Security (OPSEC) vulnerability does this disclosure represent?

answers.rationale: Social media is posting on public sites and applications; the airman here speaks privately at home rather than posting.
Open conversations are work talk in public areas or public online posts; the stem is a private talk at home.
Without clearance and need to know, family and friends should not hear job specifics or deployment details.
Text messaging is vulnerable because of open-air transmissions; the stem describes speaking in person, not sending a message.

questions.stem: Logs show a sign-in from a home internet address using credentials that were never issued to the person behind it. Which threat source does this show?

answers.rationale: An insider holds authorization to access the system; the person behind the sign-in holds none.
A botnet is an aggregation of compromised computers; the stem describes one person, not a group of controlled computers.
A third party is a subcontractor providing a product or service; the person behind the sign-in has no such role.
Outsider threats gain unauthorized or illegitimate access to a system from outside the security perimeter.

questions.stem: A flood of requests that once came from a single workstation now arrives from a hundred computers at once. Which attack type is the most specific fit?

keywords.text: from a hundred computers at once

answers.rationale: Denial of Service is the broader attack; requests from a hundred computers have a more specific name.
Unauthorized access aims at a resource the machine should not provide; the stem describes a flood of requests.
A distributed attack involves multiple computers sending requests, while a standard attack comes from one computer.
Data diddling makes small changes to records; the stem describes requests, not altered records.

questions.stem: A caller who sounds hurried and official persuades an airman to read out a password over the phone. Which attack category does this show?

keywords.text: persuades an airman to read out a password

answers.rationale: Malicious code is software or scripts written to cause undesired effects; the stem describes a phone call, not software.
Unauthorized access targets a resource the machine should not provide; the stem's caller works on a person, not a machine.
A denial of service attack sends more requests than a machine can handle; the stem reports no overload.
Psychological manipulation of people into divulging confidential information describes a caller talking an airman into revealing a password.

questions.stem: A tailored message promising confidential merger news is aimed at the very highest decision makers of a defense firm. Which attack type is the most specific fit?

keywords.text: highest decision makers of a defense firm

answers.rationale: Spear phishing is the broader type that targets any specific group; aiming at top decision makers has a more specific name.
Phishing broadcasts to a wide audience; this message is tailored to a small, senior group.
Whaling is spear phishing targeted at high-value individuals, who offer an especially high payoff for attackers.
Baiting uses curiosity or greed to trigger a trap; the stem describes a tailored message.

questions.stem: A free-music offer on a website entices visitors to install a player that secretly carries malware. Which attack type is this?

keywords.text: entices visitors to install a player

answers.rationale: Phishing acquires sensitive data through fraudulent solicitation; the stem's offer asks for no data, only an install.
Spear phishing sends messages tailored to a specific person or group; the offer here is shown to anyone.
Whaling is aimed at high-value individuals; the offer here targets anyone who sees it.
Baiting uses curiosity or greed to push a user into triggering a trap, such as installing malware onto a device.

questions.stem: An attacker is still active on three servers, and MSgt Rush cuts those servers off from the rest of the network. Which response-phase task is this?

keywords.text: cuts those servers off from the rest of the network

answers.rationale: Informing users tells people about the attack; the stem describes cutting servers off, not telling anyone.
Identifying the source traces where the attack came from; the stem describes isolating servers.
Compiling repair reports documents the affected system; the stem describes an action taken while the attacker is active.
Steps of the response phase include containing the intrusion, which fits cutting active servers off from the network.

questions.stem: A logon sends a one-time code by text message to the airman's phone, and the airman types it in. Which factor category does the code fall into?

keywords.text: text message to the airman's phone

answers.rationale: Something you know covers passwords and Personal Identification Numbers (PINs) that the user remembers, not a code delivered to a phone.
Something you are is a physical characteristic read by a biometrics system, not a delivered code.
Codes sent to mobile phones by text message are something you have, like swipe cards and physical tokens.
Something you do is a habit such as typing pattern, signature or gait, not a delivered code.

questions.stem: A phone line opens an account only when the caller's voice matches the stored voiceprint. Which factor category is the caller's voice?

keywords.text: caller's voice matches the stored voiceprint

answers.rationale: A physical characteristic such as a voice is something you are and requires a biometrics system.
Something you know is a remembered password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), not a physical characteristic.
Something you have is a card, token or texted code, not a physical characteristic.
Something you do is a habit such as typing pattern, signature or gait, not a voice.

questions.stem: A logon asks the airman to tap a smartcard and then enter a memorized Personal Identification Number (PIN). Which security concept does this combination provide?

keywords.text: smartcard and then enter a memorized

answers.rationale: Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users log on once to reach many systems; the card and Personal Identification Number (PIN) do not provide that.
Multifactor authentication uses two or more factors, such as something you have plus something you know.
Network Access Control (NAC) checks conditions systems must meet before network access, not the factors in one logon.
Accounting logs user activity and tracks usage; it does not combine factors at logon.

questions.stem: A web page asks the airman for permission to run a small component, and after approval the page can do anything on the computer. Which application vulnerability is this?

keywords.text: after approval the page can do anything

answers.rationale: Cookies hold user preferences and logon information, not take control of the computer.
Peer-to-peer file sharing moves files between users, not a component the airman approved on a page.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injects code into a web application, not a component the airman approves.
ActiveX controls can manipulate a system and obtain full system access after a user agrees to run them.

questions.stem: A system records a suspicious logon pattern on the server and emails the administrators, but it blocks nothing. Which type of security system is this?

answers.rationale: An Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) takes corrective action, which this system does not.
Network Access Control (NAC) gates network access on conditions systems must meet, not log suspicious activity.
Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users log on once for many systems, not monitor for suspicious activity.
An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) detects suspicious activity on a host or network, logs it and alerts administrators.

questions.stem: A closet holds the base's network gear and servers, and anyone walking by can open it. What measure best keeps unauthorized people away from that equipment?

keywords.text: anyone walking by can open it

answers.text: Tie them down with lockdown cables
answers.rationale: Lockdown cables secure portable devices to desks, not routers, switches and servers.
A locked safe, cabinet or drawer is for removable media and drives, not network equipment.
Routers, switches and servers should be stored in secured communications rooms or server rooms.
Storage drive encryption protects data but does not limit physical access to the equipment.

questions.stem: An airman can read, write and delete files in a folder but cannot change who else has access. Which New Technology File System (NTFS) permission adds that?

keywords.text: cannot change who else has access

answers.rationale: Full Control gives all permissions possible, including the ability to change the permissions.
Modify lets a user read, execute, delete and write, which the airman already has; it does not change permissions.
Write lets a user change file contents or create files; it does not change permissions.
List Folder Contents only shows a list of what the folder holds.

questions.stem: Between the same two Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and on the same port, MSgt Rush must allow one type of data and block another. Which security control fits?

answers.rationale: This proxy inspects the payload as well as the header, so it filters by addresses and by data type.
A stateful firewall adds conversation context to address and port filtering, not data type.
A packet-filtering firewall filters only by address and port number in the header.
A standard access list permits or denies traffic based only on the source Internet Protocol (IP) address.

questions.stem: An airman connects through a hotel's own network, and MSgt Rush's firewall rules decide what reaches the squadron's Local Area Network (LAN). Which security zone is the hotel network?

answers.rationale: A hotel's network is outside the administrator's control, so it is part of the public zone, as the Internet is.
The private zone holds the squadron's own Local Area Network (LAN) behind its firewall, not a network that a hotel runs.
The guest zone is designed for visitors to the squadron's own office location, not for a network that a hotel runs.
An extranet includes servers made accessible to selected organizations, not a network that a hotel runs.

questions.stem: An outsider signs in to a base web portal with a stolen ordinary account and sees only that account's own pages. Which event or incident category applies to this activity?

answers.rationale: Root-level intrusion involves credentials that could perform administrative functions; the stolen account here is ordinary.
Reconnaissance does not directly result in a compromise; here the outsider signed in and viewed pages.
Unauthorized non-privileged access, such as using stolen credentials for Web applications and portals, is a user-level intrusion.
An unsuccessful attempt is defeated by normal defenses; here the outsider got in and saw pages.

questions.stem: A base scheduling application is unusable for staff because attackers keep its server busy with junk requests, though no data changed. Which event or incident category applies?

keywords.text: keep its server busy with junk requests

answers.rationale: Malicious logic is adversary software installed to gain access to resources; the stem describes no installed software.
Reconnaissance gathers information that may help formulate an attack; here the application is already unusable.
An unsuccessful attempt is defeated by normal defenses; here the attack already made the application unusable.
Activity that denies, degrades or disrupts normal functionality of an information system is a denial of service.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit finished containing an intrusion but has no written roadmap showing who must do what, and by when, to restore the system. Which document is missing?

answers.rationale: The incident response plan identifies incident types and each member's job role; it is not a restoration roadmap.
The local communications focal point develops a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) with required actions and responsible offices to guide system restoration.
A Cyber Incident Report (CIR) analyzes affected systems, probable attackers, vectors and impact; it is not a restoration roadmap.
A Network Intelligence Report (NIR) focuses on a foreign threat to networks; it is not a restoration roadmap.

questions.stem: Reviewers compare a breach report against fresh logs, find that it understated the affected hosts, and correct it. Which root cause analysis step does this review perform?

keywords.text: find that it understated the affected hosts

answers.rationale: Gathering means identifying and collecting all relevant information; here the reviewers are checking a report already made.
Determining operational impact assesses effects on the mission, not the accuracy of the report.
Coordinating is working with the owning offices to set the system's category level, not correcting a report.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush notes a two-drive video-streaming volume is fast, yet losing either drive destroys all its data. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) technique is in use?

keywords.text: losing either drive destroys all its data

answers.rationale: Portions of the data are divided between two drives, which boosts performance but leaves no redundancy if either drive fails.
Each drive holds a duplicate, so losing either drive would not destroy the data.
A parity bit lets the remaining data rebuild a failed drive, so one loss would not destroy everything.
Two redundant disks let the data be rebuilt after two crashes, so nothing would be destroyed.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews a new Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) whose opening section never says what the squadron owns. Which component should that section have compiled?

keywords.text: never says what the squadron owns

answers.text: Inventory of hardware, software and data
answers.rationale: The plan begins by compiling an inventory of hardware, software applications and data.

answers.text: Analysis of natural and man-made disasters
answers.rationale: That analysis is a later planning step, not what the plan begins by compiling.
Forming the team is a planning step, not what the plan begins by compiling.
Ranking processes is a later planning step, not what the plan begins by compiling.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team has just finished assessing possible disasters and their mission impact for the squadron's Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP). Which planning step comes next?

keywords.text: assessing possible disasters and their mission impact

answers.rationale: Requirements for each department are categorized by priority right after the risk assessments.
Forming the team is the first step, already finished before any risk analysis.
Data collection comes later, after processes are ranked.
The plan is created in a standard format only after the earlier steps.

questions.stem: After MSgt Rush adds a new application, a repeat scan shows higher risk than the first scan taken at build time. Which security term names this difference?

keywords.text: higher risk than the first scan

answers.rationale: It is a change from the original baseline value, here one that increases risk.
It is a setting error that hurts performance and compliance, not the measured gap between two scans.
It is a change nobody recorded, which a before-and-after risk measurement does not describe.
It refers to service availability, not a difference between two risk measurements.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush wants the contents of files protected while they cross the network, because someone who taps the cable can read them despite file permissions. Which technology protects the contents?

keywords.text: someone who taps the cable can read them

answers.rationale: Hashing lets a receiver compare values to detect alteration; it does not hide the contents from a tap.
Encrypting the channel leaves anything tapped from the cable in an unreadable format until an authorized person decrypts it.
Backups restore data that becomes corrupt or unavailable; they do not stop a tap from reading the cable.
Clustering makes multiple servers act as one unit so another takes over after a failure; it does not conceal data on the cable.

questions.stem: A receiver accepts an order as genuine because it carries a mark made with a private key only MSgt Rush holds. Which technique provides this proof of origin?

keywords.text: a mark made with a private key

answers.rationale: Hashing compares values from the same algorithm to detect alteration, not to prove origin.
A digital signature is made with the sender's private key, which only the sender holds, so it proves the sender is who they claim.
A digital certificate transports keys; it is a file, not a mark on the order.
Encryption makes data unreadable until decrypted, not marked.

questions.stem: A shared file becomes corrupt, so MSgt Rush restores it from a copy made earlier on a regular schedule. Which high-availability practice made the restore possible?

keywords.text: restores it from a copy made earlier

answers.rationale: Patching applies service packs and hot fixes to reduce vulnerabilities; it does not provide an earlier copy of corrupt data.
Regular backups of critical information let you restore data if it becomes corrupt or unavailable.
Permissions limit who can delete data; they do not restore data once it is corrupt.
Clustering lets another server take over a workload; it does not restore a corrupt file from an earlier copy.

questions.stem: An airman who works on a classified network writes a new document and must apply its markings. Which classifier role does this airman hold?

answers.rationale: Original Classification Authority (OCA) is delegated by the Secretary of the Air Force to Air Force officials, not held by everyone with system access.
Tentative is one of the three types of classification, but it is not the status given to personnel with classified system access.
Security Managers are the contact for questions about Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) markings; system access does not make someone one.
All personnel with access to classified information systems are considered derivative classifiers, responsible for markings on documents they create.

questions.stem: Adversaries piece together a squadron's deployment date from unclassified public details such as vendor orders. Which Air Force security program addresses this exposure?

keywords.text: unclassified public details such as vendor orders

answers.rationale: Computer Security (COMPUSEC) protects information system resources and their data; it does not address an adversary piecing together mission details.
Communications Security (COMSEC) denies unauthorized persons information from government systems; the stem concerns public details, not system information.
Operations Security (OPSEC) reduces the vulnerability of missions by eliminating or reducing successful adversary collection and exploitation of critical information.
Information Security (INFOSEC) protects classified information and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI); the stem concerns unclassified public details.

questions.stem: Stored files appear as cipher text, and MSgt Rush, who holds the proper keys, needs to read them. Which operation must be performed?

keywords.text: Stored files appear as cipher text

answers.rationale: Encryption converts plain text into cipher text; the files are already in cipher text.
Steganography hides information in a graphic file; the files are cipher text, not hidden in graphics.
Hashing produces a value to detect alteration; it does not turn cipher text into readable data.
Decryption restores encrypted data to its original plain text or another readily usable state.

questions.stem: An adversary intercepts a unit's traffic without breaking its code, even though the unit uses approved cryptographic equipment correctly. Which Communications Security (COMSEC) measure would have protected the traffic?

keywords.text: intercepts a unit's traffic without breaking its code

answers.rationale: Transmission Security (TRANSEC) selects the proper secured system for communications needs, protecting intentional transmissions from interception by means other than cryptanalysis.
Cryptosecurity protects through the proper use of cryptographic systems, which the unit already does correctly.
Physical security uses barriers, limited access and approved safes for Communications Security (COMSEC) material; the stem concerns intercepted traffic.
Red/black separation partitions plain-text and encrypted signals inside equipment; it does not protect traffic from interception.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares a configuration file on a server disk with last month's approved copy and finds several values changed. Which STRIDE threat does this show?

answers.rationale: Spoofing is pretending to be another identity; the stem reports no false identity, only a file that differs.
Modifying something on a disk, network or memory describes values changed in a stored configuration file.
Repudiation is denying responsibility for an action; nobody in the stem has denied anything.
Denial of service exhausts resources so users lose service; the stem reports no loss of service.

questions.stem: A report meant only for the finance office arrives in the mailbox of an office that has no need to read it. Which STRIDE threat does this show?

keywords.text: arrives in the mailbox of an office

answers.rationale: Tampering modifies data on a disk or network; the stem reports no change to the report, only who received it.
Denial of service exhausts resources so users lose service; nothing in the stem stops working.
Spoofing is pretending to be another identity; the stem reports no false identity.
Providing information to someone not authorized to have it describes a report reaching an office with no need to read it.

questions.stem: An airman uses his own account, limited to reading files, to install software on every squadron server, a task reserved for administrators. Which STRIDE threat does this show?

keywords.text: install software on every squadron server

answers.rationale: Spoofing is pretending to be another identity; the stem keeps the airman's own account throughout.
Allowing someone to do something they are not authorized to do fits a read-only account installing software.
Disclosure gives information to someone not authorized to have it; the stem concerns installing software, not sharing information.
Repudiation is denying responsibility for an action; the stem reports no denial.

questions.stem: An airman signs in with his valid login and uses the squadron servers to run a personal side business that unit rules forbid. Which threat source does this show?

keywords.text: personal side business that unit rules forbid

answers.rationale: An outsider gains access from beyond the security perimeter; the airman here already holds valid access.
A botnet is a group of compromised computers run from a central server; the stem involves one airman's own login.
Insiders hold authorization to access a system but use it in a way that is not approved.
A third party is a subcontracted individual or company providing a service; the stem describes an airman of the squadron.

questions.stem: Opening a shared spreadsheet makes an airman's email program mail the file to every saved contact, and the code travels inside the file. Which virus type is this?

keywords.text: the code travels inside the file

answers.rationale: A boot-sector virus resides in the first sector of a disk and loads at startup; the stem's trigger is opening a file.
A macro virus is code written in a macro language that performs a malicious action and is triggered automatically when a file is opened.
A file infector attaches to executable files; the stem's code lives in a spreadsheet opened by a user.
A logic bomb stays idle until a certain event occurs; the stem's code acts as soon as the file is opened.

questions.stem: An airman installs a legitimate-looking PDF converter that works perfectly, yet afterward an unknown party starts operating the workstation from elsewhere. Which malware is this?

answers.rationale: A worm self-replicates with no user intervention; the stem has an airman choosing to install software.
A rootkit is installed on a system by a hacker; here the airman installed the converter himself.
Ransomware limits access until a ransom is paid; the stem shows no payment demand, only remote control.
A Trojan horse opens a back door on the infected machine, letting a hacker connect remotely and take control.

questions.stem: A scan on MSgt Rush's network cannot start until a client program running on the laptop signs in to the access system. Which Network Access Control (NAC) concept applies?

keywords.text: client program running on the laptop

answers.rationale: Agentless Network Access Control (NAC) needs no software on the client, but here a client program signs in first.
Agent-based Network Access Control (NAC) uses software installed on the client that authenticates the client to the NAC before scanning.
Host health checks are the scans for updates, antivirus and firewall, not the program that signs the laptop in.
Terms of usage are a statement wireless users accept, not a program on the laptop.

questions.stem: Guest laptops on MSgt Rush's network receive a scanning program when they connect, yet none remains once they disconnect. Which Network Access Control (NAC) element handles this?

answers.rationale: A dissolvable agent is installed when the laptop connects and removes itself after scanning the device for compliance.
A permanent agent keeps monitoring the system, so it would stay on the guest laptop.
Host health checks describe what is scanned for, not whether a program stays on the laptop.
Terms of usage are a statement users accept, not a scanning program.

questions.stem: Network Access Control (NAC) flags a connecting laptop because its firewall is turned off and its antivirus software is missing. Which NAC measure found those problems?

answers.rationale: Terms of usage are a statement wireless users accept, not a scan of the laptop.
A restricted network is where a failing system is placed afterward, not the scan that found the problems.
802.1X requires valid credentials before the connection, not a scan for firewall or antivirus problems.
Network Access Control (NAC) host health checks scan for Operating System (OS) updates, antivirus software and a running host-based firewall.

questions.stem: A portal on the base wireless network blocks access until an airman taps Accept on a notice. Which Network Access Control (NAC) measure does the portal apply?

answers.rationale: Host health checks scan the system for updates, antivirus and a firewall, not a statement guests accept.
A restricted network is where a failing system is placed, not a statement guests accept.
Network Access Control (NAC) may require wireless users to accept terms of usage before they get access.
802.1X requires valid credentials before the connection, not acceptance of a statement.

questions.stem: A system notices suspicious traffic aimed at a server and responds by itself instead of only reporting it. Which type of security system is this?

answers.rationale: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) detects, logs and alerts administrators, rather than responding by itself.
Network Access Control (NAC) gates network access on conditions systems must meet, not respond to suspicious traffic.
An Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) monitors for suspicious activity and takes corrective action.
Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users log on once for many systems, not respond to suspicious traffic.

questions.stem: Traffic gathered from one segment is handed to a component that decides whether any of it should raise an alert. Which Network-Based Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) component is it?

keywords.text: decides whether any of it should raise an alert

answers.rationale: A sensor collects traffic from its segment and forwards it, rather than judging the packets.
The console receives alerts and is where the administrator configures the system, not where packets are judged.
The analysis engine analyzes packets to determine whether they are suspicious.
A collector gathers traffic forwarded by sensors, rather than judging the packets.

questions.stem: A workstation reaches the Internet through a proxy, yet the airman using it believes the gateway listed in its settings is the router. Which proxy type is in use?

keywords.text: believes the gateway listed in its settings is the router

answers.rationale: With a transparent proxy the default gateway points to the proxy, and the user thinks that address is the router.
A nontransparent proxy needs a client or agent and applications pointed at it, so the setup is visible.
A reverse proxy handles requests from Internet systems to internal servers, not outbound workstation requests.
This name describes inspection of the packet payload, not a proxy the user does not know about.

questions.stem: An airman must log on to a system before any website loads, and then only some websites open for that username. Which firewall type is that system?

keywords.text: only some websites open for that username

answers.rationale: A proxy server sits between users and the Internet; users authenticate to it and it limits which websites they can visit.
A packet-filtering firewall filters by Internet Protocol (IP) address and port number, not by the username of a user.
A stateful firewall filters by address, port and conversation context, not by username.
A software-based firewall protects only the one system it is installed on.

questions.stem: The squadron lets one supplier's network, and no other outside network, reach its inventory server over the Internet. Which security zone holds that server?

keywords.text: one supplier's network, and no other outside network

answers.rationale: The Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) holds servers that the whole public must reach, not servers limited to chosen organizations.
The firewall in front of the private zone sends it no traffic from any other network, so outside organizations could not log in.
The guest zone is designed for visitors who need only Internet access, not for a server that organizations log in to.

questions.stem: A scan finds software written by attackers sitting on a workstation unnoticed, with no way for them to operate the machine live. Which event or incident category applies?

keywords.text: no way for them to operate the machine live

answers.rationale: Root-level intrusion covers malicious code that provides remote interactive control; the software here gives no control channel.
Installed adversary software that does not provide remote interactive control of the compromised system is malicious logic.
An explained anomaly is found non-malicious after investigation; adversary-written software is not non-malicious.
Denial of service degrades or disrupts normal functionality; the stem describes software sitting unnoticed, with no lost function reported.

questions.stem: An airman learns before anyone else that a virus is on one workstation. Which immediate action cuts off only that workstation while the rest of the network keeps working?

answers.rationale: Powering off the switch would cut off more than the one infected workstation.
The first responder isolates an infected computer from the network by disconnecting its network cable.

answers.text: Disconnect the base from the Internet
answers.rationale: Disconnecting the base from the Internet would isolate far more than the one infected workstation.
Requesting the hard drive is done by the Air Force Cyberspace Defense (ACD) unit for forensic analysis, not to isolate the computer.

questions.stem: Malware is spotted on several hosts, and staff isolate them to stop further spread while a deeper investigation is still pending. Which handling phase is under way?

keywords.text: isolate them to stop further spread

answers.rationale: Network technicians and incident handling personnel contain the potential threat to prevent further contamination while more detailed analysis is conducted.
Incident analysis finds what happened and the root cause; here the deeper investigation is still pending.
Response and recovery restores affected systems and follows the detailed analysis, which here is still pending.
Detection and reporting is the first phase, which comes before staff isolate hosts.

questions.stem: An airman pulls external logs, saved images and technical records into one folder for analysis. Which root cause analysis step is the airman performing?

keywords.text: pulls external logs, saved images and technical records

answers.rationale: Validating means continuously reviewing and corroborating the report for accuracy, not collecting the records.
Determining operational impact measures the effect on the mission, not collecting records.
Personnel identify and collect all relevant information for use in incident analysis, including external logs and technical information.
Coordinating is working with the owning offices to determine the system's category level, not collecting records.

questions.stem: Two of six drives crashed together, yet parity bits and the remaining data rebuilt all lost data. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) technique was in use?

keywords.text: Two of six drives crashed together

answers.rationale: Two redundant disks let the parity data and the remaining data rebuild the lost data when two drives crash.
One redundant disk rebuilds the data of only one failed drive, not two crashing together.
Mirroring keeps exact duplicates rather than using parity bits to rebuild data, which does not match this rebuild.
Dividing data between drives has no redundancy, so crashed drives would lose data permanently rather than rebuild it.

questions.stem: After the nightly job, MSgt Rush sees a single flag on each copied file change from 1 to 0. Which backup element holds that flag?

answers.rationale: A single binary digit in each file shows whether it has been backed up, and zero means it has.
Naming conventions set how backup files are labeled, not whether a copied file is flagged.
Rotation frequency sets how often backup media is swapped, not any marker on a copied file.
Storage location says where backups are kept, not which individual files were copied.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds that a weekend job copied every file and folder on a server, whether or not each file had changed. Which backup technique ran?

answers.rationale: Backing up all files and folders without relying on the archive bit copies unchanged files too.
Only data changed since the last complete copy is backed up, not every file.
Only data changed since the previous backup is copied, so unchanged files are skipped.
Vaulting is a method listed for conducting backups, not a backup type that copies everything.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's airmen carry out a recovery plan's steps against a lab copy of the network to see whether they work. Which exercise type did the airmen run?

answers.rationale: Team members validate the plan by performing scenario-based activities in a simulated environment.
Staff only discuss the procedures without applying anything, so nobody carries out the steps.
Real equipment and real personnel are used onsite, not a lab copy of the network.
It gives basic awareness training on plan contents and roles rather than performing the steps.

questions.stem: A roster that MSgt Rush saved to a shared folder is found a month later with some entries rewritten. Which security goal was broken?

answers.rationale: Confidentiality is about who can read information; the stem reports changed entries, not an unauthorized reader.
Availability is about reaching information when wanted; the file still opens, so reachability was not lost.
Nonrepudiation stops someone from disputing a sent message or change; the stem concerns altered content, not a dispute.
Data integrity means a stored file can be opened later with certainty that it was not altered while in storage.

questions.stem: An airman denies editing a shared duty roster, but the audit log records the change under the airman's account. Which concept does the audit log support?

keywords.text: the audit log records the change under the airman's account

answers.rationale: Confidentiality limits who can read information.
Availability ensures information can be reached when wanted.
Steganography hides a file in a graphic file; it does not attribute a change to an account.
Nonrepudiation ensures someone cannot dispute that they made a change, and auditing is one method used to implement it.

questions.stem: A database service keeps answering queries after one of its host machines crashes, with no action from MSgt Rush. Which high-availability solution makes this possible?

keywords.text: keeps answering queries after one of its host machines crashes

answers.rationale: Clustering has multiple servers acting as one unit, so another server takes over the workload when one fails.
Backups require a restore from an earlier copy; the stem describes service continuing with no action.
Patching reduces vulnerabilities by applying fixes; it does not move a workload after a crash.
Permissions limit who can delete data; they do not keep a service running after a crash.

questions.stem: A program on a workstation lies dormant, then wakes later and corrupts files. Under the Air Force Computer Security (COMPUSEC) program, which vulnerability category does it belong to?

answers.rationale: Unauthorized access means a person gaining entry to hardware, software or information; the stem describes a hidden program, not a person gaining entry.
Fraud, waste and abuse is intentional deception that unlawfully deprives the Air Force of value; a hidden program is not that.
Denial of service is a harm Computer Security (COMPUSEC) guards against, but it is not one of the three vulnerability categories.
The program is computer code written to cause problems that conceals itself until a later time, which is malicious logic.

questions.stem: An airman prints flyers for a personal event on a government printer without authorization. Under the Air Force Computer Security (COMPUSEC) program, which vulnerability category does this fall into?

keywords.text: flyers for a personal event on a government printer

answers.rationale: Malicious logic is code written to cause problems and conceal itself; printing flyers involves no hidden program.
Printing school car wash flyers on government resources is a listed example of fraud, waste and abuse on government computer systems.
Unauthorized access means an unauthorized person gaining entry; the stem describes no entry.
Denial of service is a harm Computer Security (COMPUSEC) guards against, not one of its three vulnerability categories.

questions.stem: A unit owns an unbreakable coding system, yet an airman skips the operating instructions that come with the equipment. Which protection is weakened?

keywords.text: skips the operating instructions that come with the equipment

answers.rationale: Transmission Security (TRANSEC) protects intentional transmissions by choosing a secured system; the stem concerns misuse of equipment, not the choice of a transmission system.
Cryptosecurity is protection from the proper use of cryptographic systems; proper use means never bypassing operational guidance.
Physical security protects Communications Security (COMSEC) material with barriers and safes; skipped instructions are not a storage lapse.
Red/black separation partitions plain-text and encrypted signals; skipped operating instructions do not involve signal routing.

questions.stem: Key material for a secure radio was left on an open desk overnight where uncleared people could walk by. Which protective measure did the lapse weaken?

keywords.text: left on an open desk overnight

answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity is the protection from the proper use of cryptographic systems; the stem concerns where material was left, not how equipment was used.
Transmission Security (TRANSEC) protects intentional transmissions by choosing a secured system; nothing in the stem was transmitted.
Password protection prevents unauthorized access to a computer system, not to material on an open desk.

textDictionary: Low latency means switches are fast: they process data very quickly, so there is little lag on the network.
A unidirectional link is traffic failing in one of two directions on a link, not two transmissions at once.
Ethernet interfaces are configured to allow connection to a Local Area Network (LAN), not to a Wide Area Network (WAN).
An exterior router directs packets between hosts in one Local Area Network (LAN) and hosts in another LAN.
Load is how busy a network resource such as a router is, not how long a packet takes to arrive.
Having no area concept is a disadvantage of Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP), not of a protocol built on areas.
Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) has no area concept, so it keeps no per-area databases.
The Transport Layer is the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer that breaks a data stream into segments, not a tier of the hierarchical model.
The core should not support workgroup access; its only purpose is moving large amounts of traffic quickly and reliably.
A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that divides the Internet Protocol (IP) address into a network address and host address.
Direct links between each pair of nodes describe a full mesh, not a star.
A broadcast storm comes from continuous broadcast traffic overwhelming the network, not from cable length.
The physical interconnection of network devices is the physical topology.
Actual procedures for a specific task are detailed in a procedure specification.
The actual arrangement of cables and hardware is what a physical network diagram shows.
Store-and-Forward, since it checks the entire frame for errors before forwarding.

Storage virtualization combines physical storage so it appears as one managed device.

Application streaming delivers needed parts of a program over the network on demand.

One adapter falls below the stated minimum for operating a host server.

Schema definitions describe allowed classes, attributes and creation rules.
